speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We are not talking about niche policies affecting some people.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We are talking about how we collectively care for parents, grandparents and other seniors whom we cherish.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We are talking about how we will be cared for when we ourselves age one day.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: That is why 24 Members of Parliament and several officeholders will be speaking about the Motions on Ageing and Caregivers today.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: For most of us, we want to see the entry into our golden years as the start of a new chapter, one in which we can age with dignity, purpose and peace of mind; one in which employment opportunities are flexible and that leverage our past experiences.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We want to continue to learn new things, contribute meaningfully and are appreciated.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We want to take life at a slower pace if we wish to, a life that is rich in meaning and where we can spend more time with the family.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We want to have the assurance that our healthcare needs are taken care of, and we know that we can count on the support of the Government and community when we need it.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: How can we achieve all of these when so few societies worldwide have succeeded, in a sustained way, through generations?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Over the past six months, Speaker Tan Chuan-Jin, as Chairperson of PAP.SG, Ms Joan Pereira, my fellow Vice-chairperson, our exco members and I did some intense consultation to explore what more can be done.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We engaged well-regarded experts in the healthcare and the ageing space, and leaders from both the Merdeka and Pioneer Generations.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We sought views from seniors from all walks of life, race and religion.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We conducted 15 forums and luncheon discussions organised in the open-ended approach similar to that of Our Singapore Conversation (OSC).

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We received online feedback and many written submissions.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: One, while an ageing society brings serious challenges, ageing should not be perceived as a problem that must be solved.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Ageing also brings many exciting and positive possibilities for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Indeed, a society can thrive and age well if it has the political will to put in place the right long-term policies.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Given that thinking long-term is a hallmark of Singapore, we should aspire to build Singapore up as one of the best places in the world to age.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Therefore, we should boldly reframe our narrative and establish a positive agenda.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Two, all of us must own our future and work together – the Government, the people and the private sector.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: No single group can succeed without the others moving together.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We must endeavour to age well as individuals and as a nation.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Three, given the diverse and evolving needs of current and future generations of seniors, the Government must continue to engage.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We found the OSC approach useful, because it builds trust, deepens engagement and generates ideas.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We must create more and more varied work opportunities for our seniors, as long as they want or as long as they are able to.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: And the key is to adopt a sector-by-sector approach and to tap on our tripartite partnership.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Five, our seniors, particularly the Merdeka Generation, have a wealth of experience.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: They want to actively volunteer their skills and time and not solely be beneficiaries.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: The Government can encourage and empower more seniors to step forward, especially through SG Cares.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Six, our Government can do more to support ground-up communities of seniors and explore increased use of dialects to better relate to our seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We recommend more age-appropriate facilities and communities for our seniors to exercise and do sports.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Eight, we must strengthen family support for seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We recommend that the Government review the definition of families to include extended families.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: If extended family members want to provide support for seniors, our policies should not be obstacles.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Nine, we need to do more to support our caregivers.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu's Motion, held concurrently today, will address that.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Ten, we can further evolve our housing policies, especially by integrating public homes with affordable assisted living services.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: The Government can facilitate the creation of group homes within public and private estates to enrich the housing choices available.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We have put our views into a position paper, which we have submitted to the Government.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: In today’s debate, these 10 points will be elaborated by all of my fellow PAP.SG Members – Ms Joan Pereira, Dr Lily Neo, Ms Tin Pei Ling, Ms Rahayu Mahzam and Miss Cheng Li Hui – as well as PAP Members passionate about senior policies.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: At this point, let me put forth an important caveat.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Our recommendations build on the excellent work already achieved.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Indeed, our seniors have been at the forefront of our Government’s and PAP’s agenda.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We can see it through at least four ways.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: In magnitude, I believe we are undergoing the most aggressive healthcare expansion and transformation in any developed country in recent memory.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Three, over the past two terms of Government, we have reforged our healthcare financing, retirement, social and public assistance system to the benefit of our seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Therefore, our debate today builds on the tremendous work of the respective terms of Government.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Now that I have set the context of this Motion, let me spend the rest of my speech on three issues: (a) improving work opportunities for our older workers; (b) strengthening our seniors' retirement adequacy; and (c) enhancing local coordination to serve our seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Here are some interesting views we have heard: one, does it make sense for companies to value us one day before our 67th birthday, and then write us off the very next day?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Two, we want to continue working, because it gives us a sense of purpose.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: But we hope to do it on our terms.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We should move away from age as a proxy for ability.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: What matters more is health status, our state of mind.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: At the same time, we hear other viewpoints: some seniors work to stay financially independent, or to supplement their income; others work because they need a certain amount of money to retire with dignity.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Given such diverse views, we believe Singapore’s objective must be to create more, and more varied, work opportunities for our seniors, as long as they want, or as long as they are able to.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: How does reality match up to this objective?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We offset employers’ cost of hiring older worker through the Special Employment Credit.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We have tightened standards for companies to bring in non-Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: But there is always a higher mountain to climb, a higher peak to aspire to.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We believe there is room to evolve our approach.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Moving forward, the solution is not to solely or even largely depend on putting more legislation compelling firms to hire more seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Rather, we must create win-win situations so that older workers benefit, companies benefit and Singapore benefits, for both today and tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Therefore, we recommend a sector-by-sector, tripartite approach to systematically apply the policies to create more full-time and part-time opportunities for our seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: And we must also help older workers better access freelance opportunities.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Especially within fast-growing industries like information technology (IT), healthcare, logistics and transportation, there is room for more full-time jobs for our older workers.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We must put the employment of older workers firmly on the agenda of these industries and have more focus discussions and sharing of success stories at the sector and industry level.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: And through these focus discussions, we must encourage companies and unions to tap on: (a) Job Redesign+ grants to automate jobs, so that older workers can handle easily; (b) training and internship grants to onboard older workers from other industries; and (c) human resource (HR) grants to implement policies friendly to workers who are older.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Over time, we hope that all 23 Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) will do the same.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Of course, some will call this approach incremental.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Incremental policies, if pursued diligently and intelligently, can yield solid and sustained results.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: And this approach draws on Singapore’s strength, which is the strong spirit of partnership among our unions, companies and the Government.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Next, we call for all companies to adopt flexible work arrangements (FWAs) when possible.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: This helps older workers who desire to work, but on the terms and at a pace that they are comfortable with.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: By FWAs, we mean flexible locations, time and load.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We should encourage the vast majority of companies to create many more formal FWA roles.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: More FWA roles mean more part-time jobs and benefiting our older workers.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: They can retain and hire talented older workers who prefer or require FWA.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: They will be well-positioned to navigate through our constrained labour market.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Also, as Singapore continues to strengthen our social services, we call on the Government to create more part-time opportunities.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: For example, there can be more part-time roles, such as adjunct teachers, Senior Generation Ambassadors, medical befrienders, community organisers, assistants to visiting nurses and enforcement officers.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: But we call for a whole-of-Government approach to adopt FWA.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: It will also free up more young Singaporeans for the private sector.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We just have to put our heads together and take this to the next level.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: PAP.SG further calls on our companies, unions and the Government to study other countries’ experience in promoting FWA, including legislation on "right-to-ask" for FWA.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Next, we need to empower our older workers to access freelance opportunities.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: The rise of the platform economy, also called the gig-economy, creates more freelance opportunities for our older workers.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: One, food delivery services, such as Foodpanda and GrabFood.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Just last week, Janice Tai from The Straits Times estimates that there are more than 600 seniors doing freelance food delivery.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: TMC builds on Singaporean women's own experience as grandmothers and mothers and equips them with the latest health and confinement culinary skills and then place them as freelance confinement nannies.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: It helps older professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) from the financial sector transit into freelance consultants, board directors and even advisors to charities.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: It has received support from Workforce Singapore's (WSG's) Professional Conversion Programme, and Singapore Consultancy is a model worth encouraging.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We expect the platform economy to grow, but older workers need more help to access these freelancing opportunities.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Take the food delivery business as an example.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: On the ground, I sometimes meet very fit seniors in their late 60s and even 70s who want a job but cannot get one.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: At the same time, major food delivery companies have no upper age limit, because they do not see significant differences in performance and safety records between younger and older freelance workers.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We call on WSG, the Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) and the unions for self-employed persons (SEPs) to do more to teach our seniors digital literacy, and direct suitable healthy seniors to these opportunities, including through digital platforms, such as the new National Trades Union Congress (NTUC)-IBM portal.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Beyond food delivery, there are many other freelance opportunities, especially in professional services, as well as food and beverage (F&B) industries.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: For some older workers, the reality is that it will be hard, though not impossible, for them to get full-time opportunities.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Therefore, we recommend WSG and e2i to not just position older workers for full-time jobs in their current sectors but also help them identify transferable skills for part-time and freelancing opportunities in other sectors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: In addition, the Government and SEP unions can jointly create a positive environment for SEPs through ensuring fair contracting terms, strengthening medical coverage, improving access to training grants and facilitating CPF contributions.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We can also do more to remove obstacles for our older workers to continue working.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: In particular, certification tests are becoming necessary for more jobs.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Some older workers fail these tests and have to downgrade to lower-paying jobs.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Therefore, we call on the Government to encourage best practices for testing seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: These can include using larger fonts in tests, providing seniors with more time for computer-based tests, allowing seniors with relevant working experience to take written or oral tests in Chinese, Malay and Tamil.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: In addition, we should also equip our workers from 40 years old onwards with future skills, after which it may become progressively harder to learn radically different skills.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: A good example is SkillsFuture's TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA) programme, which has recently incorporated future skills, such as deep machine learning.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: With longer lives and smaller families, Singaporeans need to save more and plan better for retirement, especially for workers above 55 and SEPs who do not contribute to their CPF Special Account.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Therefore, a measured way to do this is important.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: But it is the right thing to do.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Over time, we should consider asking SEPs to build up their CPF Special Account.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: CPF’s interest rate is already higher than market interest rates and this is already a natural incentive.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Four, we recommend continued support for low-income seniors through the WIS Scheme and the Silver Support (SSS) Scheme.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Five, we recommend that the Government accelerate collaborations with community partners to help Singaporeans plan for retirement.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We call for the Post Office Savings Bank (POSB) and NTUC to consider setting up a Thrift and Loan co-operative for seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, let me touch on enhancing local coordination to serve our seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: I believe that the frontier of social work in Singapore, including caring of our seniors, lies in helping those in need in a multi-pronged and integrated manner; getting the community to step in when the family nucleus fails, solving issues upstream through policy and community intervention, and shaping societal norms that are caring and empowering.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We at PAP.SG believe strong local coordination is critical to achieving these goals.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: At the local level, because we have a holistic view of the various needs, we can seek both local and national resources to meet these needs.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: So, today, some of my PAP colleagues will also share on their local efforts.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Putting a spotlight on these programmes will, hopefully, create a cascading effect nationwide.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Kembangan-Chai Chee has integrated social work efforts, where their volunteers work with voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) and agencies.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Here are two of their many programmes where seniors in need are involved.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Two, help for families with mental health issues, including hoarding.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: The team from Kembangan-Chai Chee partners the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) and the Institute of Mental Health (IMH), and acts as their ground volunteers.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: As we all know, cases involving families with mental health issues are usually complex.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: It takes time and many partners to collaborate on each case, but the volunteers there press on to do the necessary.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: In Henderson-Dawson where Ms Joan Pereira serves, residents also work with Willing Hearts to provide daily meals to fellow residents in need, including many seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: For our frail and socially-isolated seniors who need help, our team of volunteers from Project Starfish are able to assist every single of them through: (a) regular befriending by well-trained volunteers who work with agencies and VWOs to meet the needs of seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Next, for our seniors at Kebun Baru who are looking for a place to bond and do exercise, we have set up a Senior Activity Centre through the kind assistance of Methodist Welfare Services.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Two local churches have also opened up communal spaces for our seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We are also working with the Alzheimer's Dementia Association to build a dementia-friendly Kebun Baru.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Moving forward, we would like to work with Active SG to bring in more communal sports, especially for our senior men.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: I look forward to hearing about other local efforts from Members of this House.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: I also spoke about creating work opportunities and strengthening retirement adequacy for seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, I spoke about how effective local coordination can help us better care for and empower our seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Ultimately, I hope that all Singaporeans can realise that we can collectively build Singapore up as one of the best places in the world to age.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu will now put forth a Motion about supporting our caregivers.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In accordance with the decision of this House to jointly take this Motion and the next Motion standing in the name of Dr Chia Shi-Lu, I will now call Dr Chia to move his Motion and make his opening speech before allowing Members to debate on both Motions.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Why are we focusing on such family caregiving or informal caregiving?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Over the course of the Chinese New Year festivities last week, as I made my way through rounds of family and constituency celebrations, I was heartened to observe strong family ties and the special care paid to the elderly.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Gatherings are centred around the seniors, with extended family members coming together to pay their respects to their 长辈, or their seniors – grandparents, granduncles and grand-aunties: "恭喜发财, 身体健康".

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: All of these were said with sincerity and with genuine well-meaning.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But in every situation, the infirm elderly were treated with care and respect, with love and concern, and quite naturally so, showing that such caregiving has already become part of the fabric of the tapestry that is family.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Traditional values are still strongly held in our society and the family remains the first line of support.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: A majority of Singaporeans prefer to care for elderly family members themselves.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is the same whether you are Chinese, Malay, Indian or Eurasian.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Fewer seniors are placed in institutional care, and this is only usually due to extenuating circumstances.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Our seniors also prefer to stay in familiar surroundings near or surrounded by their children and grandchildren.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The desire to experience "天伦之乐" or the joy of family ties, is universal.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This arrangement is mutually beneficial for the young and old.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As our children participate in the process of providing care for the elderly, they imbibe important values, such as filial piety, responsibility, respect, compassion and empathy.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They learn most and they learn best from our personal examples.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As our family sizes shrink and life expectancies increase, the task of caregiving for elderly members will become more challenging.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The load on each caregiving party will become heavier and the last lap for each senior is expected to last longer.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While we all aim to help our seniors stay healthy for as long as possible, we must also prepare for frailty, a growing chronic disease burden, and the prevalence of dementia.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In view of the rising needs of family caregivers, it is timely for us to review areas of support for caregivers.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We need a whole-of-society approach – the Government, the community, families and individuals.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We all have a part to play in supporting caregivers and our seniors.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This means that they have to juggle work commitments, family responsibilities and caregiving.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Caregiving certainly had a negative impact on these working caregivers.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How can we then help these caregivers in an increasingly competitive and demanding work environment?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The Nordic countries, Australia and Canada already offer paid leave for working caregivers.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In Singapore, paid leave is only for childcare.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Employees may also tap on six days of unpaid leave for infants.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I would think that compared to the occasional days of eldercare or caregiver leave, FWA has a greater impact on a caregiver's ability to continue working.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In fact, a body of research in OECD countries have found this to be exactly the case.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We must support those who would like to remain in the workforce.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Otherwise, not only would our economy suffer from the loss of their skills and knowledge, their loss of income would have a negative impact on their families' finances and their own futures as seniors.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) should consider committing additional resources to speed up the adoption of FWA and to increase awareness among jobseekers and employees of companies with FWA.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I understand that under the Enhanced Work-Life Grant, companies can already apply for grants and incentives to implement job sharing and FWAs, such as flexi-load, flexi-place and flexi-time.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: One of my concerns is that companies may be deterred by the amount of administrative work and changes to work processes in order to integrate FWA.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Another obstacle would be the additional financial costs to the company.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For example, for job sharing, a company would have to hire two instead of one worker.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Due to the cap on CPF contributions, it may cost a company less to hire one full-time worker than to hire two, each with correspondingly lower salaries but which attract employer CPF contributions below the cap.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Similarly, employers may have to pay double for employees' insurance premiums.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It would be helpful for MOM to have dedicated liaison officers to examine all these potential roadblocks with interested or perhaps with targeted companies and work on overcoming these barriers together.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So far, the implementation of FWA has been employer-centric.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I wonder if it is possible for the FWA framework to become more employee-centric.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For organisations which are not proactive, what can employees do?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would the Ministry consider setting up a channel to enable employees to appeal for FWA to MOM directly?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Upon receipt of such a request, MOM may then send a liaison officer to discuss with the company the viability of FWA and share the successful experiences of other companies.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Next, I would like to appeal for greater support for respite care, particularly emergency respite care.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Respite care schemes provide much-needed temporary breaks for caregivers.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Although most families choose to take care of their elderly, there would be times when the emotional and physical demands of such caregiving take their toll, especially when the seniors suffer from poor health or mental issues.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Planned respite care offers the opportunity for caregivers to rest and recharge.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Research overseas have also shown that regular breaks from caregiving is beneficial to family caregivers' health and well-being and reduce conflict between spouses and also among family members.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Respite care can also help to reduce abuse or neglect of the elderly and delay or prevent seniors from being sent to institutionalised care subsequently.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These centres should also be linked so that, if they have no vacancies, they may make referrals to the nearest centres.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I understand that the United Kingdom (UK) and Australia already have such systems in place.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Private companies and non-profit organisations can continue to run similar set-ups to provide a wider range of choices for families.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In various surveys of caregiver concerns, the one issue that keeps on sticking out is financial stress.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Over the last few years, the idea of providing an allowance to family caregivers has surfaced episodically.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While the Government provides subsidies for home and community care through schemes, such as Silver Support and the Senior Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF), caregivers still have to incur out-of-pocket costs for consumables, medication, transportation and others.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For those who have left their jobs to look after the elderly full-time, additional financial support would be helpful and is, in fact, needed.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The concern here is over the long-term financial sustainability of paying family caregivers as the number of elderly increases even as the number of Singaporeans in the workforce shrinks.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Countries which implement payouts, such as UK, Australia and Hong Kong, limit this benefit to lower-income caregivers or to caregivers with no other sources of income.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In Mandarin):  	Now, I would like to talk about how we can improve our caregivers' capabilities.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: All caregivers require easy access to information and training to enable them to provide care competently for their loved ones.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As far as possible, the Government should simplify these chunks of information and provide them in mother tongues and dialects as well.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many caregivers are themselves elderly and it can be quite confusing for them to process so much information.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We can also draw upon community resources, such as volunteers from neighbourhood groups, who can be trained to disseminate information and translation to support the one-stop centres.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These volunteers can also be part of caregiver support groups which they can turn to for social and emotional support.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Whether online or classroom training, sessions should be conducted in multiple languages so that everyone, including foreign domestic workers (FDWs), would be able to understand easily and learn in bite-size modules to accommodate different schedules.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In English): In conclusion, Mr Speaker, caring for a senior is a whole-of-society effort.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Now is a timely opportunity for the Government, for our community and for individuals to come together and study ways to improve support for our caregivers and help our fellow Singaporeans age with dignity.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In accordance with the decision of this House to have a simultaneous debate on both Motions, I would now call the Members to make their speeches.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, Members are allowed to consider both Motions in a single speech.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: I spoke on the need to plan in advance and better prepare in the provision of healthcare and social needs.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Today, 22 years later, this topic is still relevant, with increasing pertinence.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: And I am glad that many Members of this House are speaking up on this area and in support of it.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: I have been an advocate on the promotion of quality life for seniors all these years as the main basis of the best way forward for successful ageing in our population.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: The aim is for seniors to live healthily and happily with good physical, mental and social well-being, for as long as possible, with the promotion of healthy lifestyles.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: This is the reason for the four Senior Activity Centres (SACs) in Kreta Ayer-Kim Seng Constituency for the last 20 years.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: The other aim is delaying and limiting the disabilities in the seniors, by preventing diseases and detecting diseases early and treating them early, to prevent complications of diseases.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Our Government had acknowledged the importance of healthy living for a happy populace, through the promotion of healthy lifestyles, to be adopted by seniors.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Thus, the island-wide community Active Ageing, under the People's Association's (PA's) Wellness Programme for seniors, is now adopted by almost all Residents' Committees (RCs).

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: In the area of preventing disabilities, the Ministry of Health (MOH) had also emphasised on the prevention of chronic diseases, an example of which is the recent campaign on the "War on Diabetes".

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Hopefully, with preventive healthcare approaches as above, we can keep seniors as healthy and happy and reducing disability for as long as possible.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: But inevitably, many, if not all, seniors will become frail, especially towards the end of their lives.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: These ADLs are dressing, eating, toileting, transferring and continence.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Today, I want to focus my speech on seniors who require assistance in their daily living due to frailty or disability.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: These seniors need caregivers to enable them to live with dignity.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: With Singapore’s demographic profile, especially going forward, many people are required to provide these caring roles for dependent seniors.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: The report on the survey of Informal Caregiving in Singapore showed that in 2010, 8.1% of Singapore residents aged between 18 and 69 indicated that they provided regular care or assistance to friends or family members.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Some 37% of caregivers reported that they had been providing care to their care recipients for over a decade.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: According to this survey, close to three-quarters of caregivers, or 74%, were in employment.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Surveys in other countries had shown that many caregivers face challenges with financing constraints, with juggling between jobs and their caregiving roles and, in some, with having to look after their young children as well.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: They contribute much to their family members, friends and community.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Their deeds are commendable and they need to be better acknowledged and supported with better Government policies in place.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: To give financial support for dependent seniors will help them cope with daily living and lessen the burdens of their caregivers.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Financial support is an important and integral part of help to achieve the desired outcome.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: I favour the monthly remuneration to these eligible care recipients.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: This amount should be commensurate with the amount required to pay for a full-time domestic helper to assist with daily activities for dependent seniors.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: ElderShield's criteria are just as stringent, with three ADL deficits before being eligible.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Many seniors are also not on ElderShield and the new CareShield's premiums are out of reach for most seniors.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: I, therefore, urge our Government to better provide our seniors with a better financing grant.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: I hope the existing grants will not be removed even with any new grants.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Two, facilitating seniors to age in place in the community.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Many seniors have expressed that they prefer to live for as long as possible in their own homes, in the familiar environment and in the community with old friends.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Many do value the joy of living with their family members.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: We should also encourage the community to come together to make this work.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Kreta Ayer-Kim Seng constituency has such a grounds-up grassroots and community initiative.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: It is called Ageing Gracefully at Home (AGH).

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: This was set up in 2014 in the Chin Swee Housing and Development Board (HDB) rental blocks and now also extended to the Kreta Ayer HDB rental blocks.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: AGH is a holistic care programme carried out by half a dozen full-time caregivers who include nurses for the frail seniors with mobility disability living alone at the rental blocks.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: These disabled seniors do not have family caregivers and cannot afford domestic helpers.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Under AGH, home visits are provided for these frail seniors with the following services: daily supervision on meals, blood pressure checks, medicine intake, home cleaning services, bathing, identifying people who are sick, medical assistance, hospital transportation and so on.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Able-bodied residents of the blocks are remunerated in kind to provide befriending services to those disabled residents.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: VWOs are roped in to provide the assistance to the seniors to fill the gaps.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Since its inception, I noticed that more seniors could remain in their own rental homes.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: There were lesser fatalities in these homes with lesser admissions to hospitals.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: More importantly, residents are happier living and ageing gracefully in their own homes with AGH-assisted programmes.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: I hope the Government can look into similar models to benefit more seniors in other precincts.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: I also hope that the caregiver support grant which I proposed earlier can be extended to the community caregivers, such as AGH, to look after seniors with needs better.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: The purpose of homecare is to enable seniors with medical conditions to remain in their own homes.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: This is especially useful after their discharge from hospitals.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Under homecare, MOH can facilitate services, such as medical caregiving, nursing, medication, nutrition, occupational therapy, rehabilitation therapy and other domiciliary services in seniors’ homes.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: This is a better step-down care approach, which will improve outcome of residents coping at home.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Many family members, usually caregivers themselves, have told me that they were apprehensive and concerned that they would not be able to cope with their family members who are just discharged from hospitals.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: To better equip caregivers, it is thus good practice to ensure family members get the information and support they need at this early stage, before discharging patients to their own homes, and to hold caregivers’ hands in managing their care recipients at their own homes subsequently.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Many employed caregivers have expressed difficulty balancing between holding demanding jobs with their caregiving roles.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: By so doing, the Government will send the right message, in an ageing population, on the importance of empathy for the caring roles of caregivers.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Such paid "Care Leave" can be two weeks, for a start, similar to "Parental Leave".

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: FWAs should be encouraged and incentivised in our workforce.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Government Ministries should take the lead to implement it.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: This will improve caregivers' employability, with less frequent absenteeism and lack of concentration at work.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Caregivers can suffer burnout syndrome from emotional and physical fatigue.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Respite care can be further made more readily available for caregivers to better perform their roles.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Social Service Offices (SSOs) should be the one-stop centre for information and respite care referrals for caregivers.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: AIC can station their staff at the SSOs to provide this role.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: The pricing for respite care services can be daunting for those without subsidy.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: A family with an average income of $5,000 may have to fork out almost $1,000 for one-week respite care.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Many caregivers are interested to take up courses to better equip themselves for their roles.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: If multiple caregivers of the same care recipient wish to attend the training, the $200 would need to be shared amongst them.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Most home training courses cost $200 for the basic two-hour training.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: I hope MOH can make caregiving training more accessible and affordable.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: The majority of people aspire to continue to live in their own homes as they age.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Housing adaptability to accommodate seniors’ mobility as they progress in years, as well as having a senior-friendly environment in the vicinity, will enable them to live their normal lives for as long as possible without having to rely on others.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Examples of housing adaptability are the installation of ramps and grab-bars, having space and doors for motorised mobility aids, non-slip bathrooms, appropriate-height kitchen tabletops, hoisting aids to get out of beds, emergency call points and so on.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Technology adaptability, such as smart home aids for seniors, fall sensors, emergency medical detection sensors and so on, should be used to enhance their quality of life.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: A friendly environment in the vicinity of seniors’ homes should have food centres, health facilities and wellness centres with barrier-free access to these places.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Every few blocks should have at least one Senior Activity Centre to promote physical, mental and social wellness of the seniors.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: I urge our Government to build new homes at the outset of public housing construction to be “future-proofed” for the consideration of independent living for seniors.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: Three speeches ago, I said that "it is not so much what is said, but what is done, that will be the measure of our progress." Together with others in this House, I look forward to the Government’s continuing efforts to lend support to our caregivers.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: There are different types of caregivers: some are paid for their caregiving, others are not and we call them informal caregivers.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: They take care of family members or relatives who are young, who are disabled or who are seniors.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: Today, I will talk about informal caregivers who take care of seniors.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: In many ways, informal or unpaid caregivers enable other Singaporeans to carry out the economic activities that are counted in our gross domestic product (GDP), while their own caregiving is not.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: As of now, the burden of informal caregiving falls disproportionately on women.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: Our dependence on this group of Singaporeans is real, substantial and very often unacknowledged.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: It is well‐documented that caregivers often suffer declines in their own financial circumstances and mental and physical health.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: But, Sir, almost half of our informal caregivers to seniors do not work at other jobs, often precisely because of the unpaid caregiving responsibilities that they have taken on, to their financial detriment and reduced retirement adequacy.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: We understand that the Government is reviewing enhancing caregiver support in areas, such as respite services, and working with community partners to offer more socio-emotional support to caregivers.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, Sir, "When the Great Way prevails, public society is shared equally by the people." In the society of "Great Harmony, the aged is provided for till their end, the able-bodied find employment, the young are nurtured, and the widowed and the disabled are cared for." Well, in our society, the burden of looking after the old, the young and the disabled falls mainly on female members of the family.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: Often, they themselves are old, and look after an even older member of the family.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: Influenced by traditional gender stereotypes, the spouse and the unmarried grown-up daughter are often seen as natural candidates as caregivers to seniors, with their own needs often neglected.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: While their caregiving is not included in economic data – not counted in the GDP – it brings real stress and burden that can lead to limited social life, stunted personal development, including career development, as well as declines in physical and mental health.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Therefore, we need to support caregivers, both to give them the much-needed respite as well as financial help.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In the constituency I serve, we see caregivers who are not working but are caring for their aged parents fulltime.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In the workplace, we see people who work during the day and return at home to give care to their parents who are aged.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: To provide respite for the caregivers, there needs to be people who can stand in to care for the elderly while the primary caregiver is taking a much-needed respite to rest and be recharged.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Besides training courses that are geared towards equipping primary caregivers with the necessary skills, what is also important is training courses for others to learn the skills.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This would allow others to provide flexible home-based care so that primary caregivers can enjoy the weekly respite they need.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Another important way in which caregivers can be supported is through caregiver leave and FWAs.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This will help those who feel the need to accompany their aged parents for medical checkups.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Other times, when an aged parent unexpectedly falls ill, such measures will allow caregivers to have the peace of mind in knowing that they will have the ability to address emergencies on the home front.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: To support caregivers financially, there can be greater subsidies or Government contributions for home-based care assistants working in VWOs.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is important so that our seniors can choose to age well at home, in an environment that is conducive, comfortable and convenient.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is to recognise the sacrifices made by primary caregivers as well as the crucial contributions they make.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Lower levies do not benefit those who may not be able to afford FDWs.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Institutional subsidies are unable to support those who are cared for at home.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, these Motions are timely to help address some of these gaps.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is in line with the reason cited in the ElderShield Review Committee Report as to why cash reimbursements should be provided so that it will provide claimants and their caregivers the flexibility to decide on their desired care arrangements.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Any financial help for the person being cared for will, in turn, benefit the caregiver, whether the caregiver is a family member or a person who is paid.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If the caregiver is a family member, the financial relief can be used in ways which would otherwise be used to provide care for the person cared for.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If the caregiver is a person being paid, that caregiver can be paid better.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But this is not just a call for practical action, but also a principled statement.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: A statement that we need to care for all – the young, the middle-aged, the elderly.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Because we believe that every person is precious no matter what their age.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Everyone should be able to age with dignity.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Just because a person is not working or unable to take care of themselves or may not be mentally alert does not mean that the person is not valued in society.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: That is why we want to create more policy space so that our elderly can age with dignity, financially supporting them and their caregivers.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Again, this brings home the point about why both the Motions today are timely.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We should not in any way regard the elderly as a burden.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I hope that this Motion will give the elderly the message that they are respected and looked up to.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The elderly have a special place in the community and we have a lot to learn from them.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is the reason why, in my constituency, we have situated an infant care centre, childcare centre as well as a senior care centre near one another.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We are planning various initiatives for both groups of people – the children with their parents and the seniors with their caregivers – to interact meaningfully with each other, for example, having combined celebrations of the different festivities, interactions during the year-end childcare celebrations as well as introducing grandparents' week.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: What we want is for them to have fruitful interactions with one another to strengthen the imparting of good moral values, such as kindness, caring and respect.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, what we are debating in Parliament today is a reflection of the high position we give the elderly in our community.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Furthermore, this is a good first step to recognising the valuable contributions and unique challenges that caregivers face.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I feel that we can and should look beyond caregivers of the elderly.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In my constituency, I have witnessed the great courage of parents and family members of those who are physically or mentally challenged.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: They have a great weight on their shoulders.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Sometimes, unfortunately, the father leaves and the caregiving duties fall fully on the mother.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For those who care for these children with special needs, much care is taken to create a protective environment in the home for the child.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But what that means is that there is very little downtime for the caregivers themselves.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Caregiving is a 24/7 job, except when the person cared for is sleeping, which is when the caregivers sleep, too.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: They, too, need to be able to rest and recharge emotionally, physically, mentally.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But often, there is no opportunity for the much-needed respite.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: A single mother in Ulu Pandan, the constituency I serve, takes care of her special needs child.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We were in contact for a number of years, partnering her family and supporting them.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: One day, she shared with me that she has another child, a daughter, who was getting married and asked whether we would be able to arrange care for her teenage son with special needs so that she can attend her daughter's wedding.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As there was no one who could help care for her son during that time and her son needed specialised, close supervision, she was prepared not to attend her daughter’s wedding.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: That struck me – the level of commitment and dedication of that mother.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Because her son had a tendency to harm himself, we made special arrangements with a hospital to care for him for those two days on which the wedding took place.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: After the wedding, she continued to take care of her son at home.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: She recently broke the happy news to me that she is now a grandmother – her daughter gave birth.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Nevertheless, it is not my purpose to distract from the good starting block that we are at now, in particular, caring for the caregiver of the elderly.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The community needs to support ageing with dignity.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: While some caregivers may be married and have a reservoir of extended family who can come in at least once in a while and support, others who did not get married may not have such resources available.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I am confident that MOH, the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) and the Government will put in place measures that will benefit and provide the much-needed support for our seniors – our seniors who helped to build the Singapore we have today to age with dignity, and to provide their caregivers with key support mechanisms.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The Motion on "Ageing with Purpose" is a follow-up on the position paper "Empowering Us to Live with Purpose and Dignity in Our Senior Years" submitted by the PAP Seniors Group.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Under Speaker Tan Chuan-Jin’s guidance, my Parliamentary colleague Mr Henry Kwek and I completed this position paper with the support and feedback of seniors from all walks of life and experts in healthcare and ageing.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With longer life expectancies, many of our seniors and, in the near future, we ourselves, will be looking at a much longer period of our lives spent in old age.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: There will be physiological changes and, hence, adjustments to policies and infrastructure are necessary.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We require repurposing, from providing smaller assisted-living (AL) flats with shorter leases to programming longer "green man" time for crossing roads.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Active ageing requires support from both the Government and society.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For many seniors, it is important for them to keep their independence and to age in place.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We will need to provide more AL options in both HDB and private housing.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We would like to appeal for senior Group Homes with AL facilities within HDB estates.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We can either utilise available void deck space, where suitable, or transform several combined HDB flats into a senior Group Home with AL facilities.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Like The Henderson Home in Henderson-Dawson ward where I serve, the flats and a senior activity centre are served by staff members on call and a resident carer.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We hope that Kampung Admiralty’s concept of locating senior housing together with medical facilities, transportation, shopping and other amenities can be duplicated in new estates and on available land in older ones.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Next, I would like to suggest that we build more SACs at locations within walking distance of seniors’ flats and apartments.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This concept would be similar to the Wellness Kampungs where seniors can do exercises and take part in various activities, such as digital literacy, while at the centre, and senior volunteers may step forward to help if they wish.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Exercising in a group will provide the motivation for our elders to keep up with their friends’ and neighbours' fitness levels.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: On the other hand, digital tools will increasingly dominate almost every aspect of our lives.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We, therefore, wish to see better programmes aimed at helping seniors to improve their digital literacy, in ways which can help to value-add to and improve their quality of life.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We must not leave anyone behind in moving forward as a smart nation and should provide more support to help our seniors go digital.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With an increasing number of seniors, we need to boost SAC’s or Wellness Kampungs' capacity in both HDB and private estates.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Having such centres near to their residences will encourage our elderly to take part in the activities there more frequently.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The proximity will allow seniors to easily walk home and rest without worrying about transportation.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Their families will also have peace of mind knowing that there will be someone keeping an eye on their parents and even grandparents.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We are advocating for a "many helping hands approach" to help us Singaporeans age well.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And the most important pair of hands belongs to one's family.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Our family sizes are shrinking due to a falling birth rate, and this means that there are fewer "hands" around who are considered immediate family members.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In Mandarin):   We are advocating for a "many helping hands" approach to help us Singaporeans age well.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And the most important pair of hands belongs to one's family.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Our family sizes are shrinking due to a falling birth rate, and this means that there are fewer "hands" around who are considered immediate family members.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How about helping hands from extended family members?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Therefore, we are proposing to broaden the definition of family members in Government policies to better allow Singaporeans to help support their extended family members if they wish.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: If the extended family member wishes to help, our policies should encourage it.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We would like to suggest that extended members of a family be allowed to contribute to one another’s account, for example, from grandchildren to grandparents.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Familial ties run deep in our society, even amongst extended family members.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We should recognise and support the efforts of caregivers, who can be part of the extended family.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Such forms of support can also help to reduce the number of isolated elderly in our midst, given that there are isolated elderly who do not have children but may still have extended family members who can and wish to help out.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But it is also one of the most physically and emotionally draining tasks on earth.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Next, on volunteerism, a topic very close to my heart.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Volunteering is one of the key hallmarks of active ageing.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Elderly volunteerism or senior volunteerism will allow our elderly to stay active and engaged in the community.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The regular interaction also enables them to look out for one another, make new friends and strengthen kinship amongst neighbours.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We believe volunteering will lead to well-being and good health for our seniors.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Our seniors' wisdom, talent, wealth of experience and strong moral values make them very suitable for volunteering.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They are generally more patient and, hence, suitable as mentors to younger volunteers.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am particularly keen for such intergenerational volunteering efforts to succeed as we should encourage and strengthen bonding between the young and old.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope that our community can actively reach out to our seniors when recruiting volunteers.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We all have our passions and calling and, given the chance to volunteer in our areas of interest, we will gladly bring our expertise and knowledge to serve.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I know of a resident in her 70s, Lucy is her name, who initiated a neighbourhood citizens patrol group because she was worried about the safety within her estate.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Whether it is a hospital, museum or school, I hope our public, private and charity organisations can keep a special lookout for the "silver pool" as a volunteer resource.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I trust many of us, as Members of Parliament, would have received requests for assistance from seniors regarding their employment.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Many of my older residents who have come to see me shared their challenges either in staying employed or finding a new job.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Some need to stay employed as they still need to pay for their living expenses.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Many are usually still capable of working, have a wealth of knowledge and experience and can still contribute to various industries.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I believe, at times, there are mismatched expectations.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I have heard feedback from some employers who have concerns about hiring seniors.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It may be less cost-effective to employ an older worker who expects the same amount of pay that he or she is used to but may not be able to accept a bigger scope of work.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The inherent assumption is that a younger employee who is hungry for a challenge may be less demanding and be willing to put in extra hours, for less pay.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Further, there may be difficulties promoting and advancing the careers of younger employees if the older workers do not "make space".

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In this regard, the Government’s efforts in introducing various policies and schemes over the past decade have helped.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I acknowledge that without all these policies and schemes, the employment situation for the elderly workers may be more challenging.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I believe though that, as a community, we can and must continue to work towards combating any discrimination against older workers and create an even more conducive job market for them.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There is a need to continue to support and encourage employers to see the benefits of employing older workers and guide them towards redesigning jobs and creating work arrangements that could be a win-win for all.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The Government could work with unions, grassroots leaders or other industry stakeholders to create support platforms that would help push and further encourage the adoption of existing grants and schemes so that more seniors can be employed.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: These platforms could also incorporate opportunities for open discussions with older workers about the needs of the industry or sector so that we could also work towards shifting mindsets of older workers and manage their expectations.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I believe that with a little more effort and support, we can change the current job landscape for our older workers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The second point I would like to touch on is the living environment for the elderly.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In this regard, it is noted that the approach taken with the Kampung Admiralty development is very commendable.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Moving forward, we would also have to consider the fact that the elderly group is quite diverse and may have different needs and preferences, depending on their family make-up and their financial situation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: To ensure that Singaporeans, now and in the future, are able to age with purpose and dignity, I believe we should look at ensuring that there would be options for different living arrangements.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: One option is group homes or retirement homes with AL facilities, something mentioned by my colleague, Ms Joan Pereira, earlier.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I believe this is where we can take a whole-of-community approach and encourage developers from the private sector to step up.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I note that there was an attempt at this model with one of the developments at Jalan Jurong Kechil, which is in my estate.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The development was slated to be a potential retirement village.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The idea was noble but, now that it is developed, many have questioned whether it is just a typical condominium as there were no real guidelines on who the units were sold to.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We may want to revisit and refine this model.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This could mean creating a new strata title category and legislation which could ringfence non-seniors from purchasing such properties and deal with the conversion or transfer of ownership upon demise of the owners.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This could mean, as Ms Joan Pereira mentioned, converting several HDB units to form a group home with AL facilities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This may be one way where the seniors could stay within familiar areas and be close to their families.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The other aspect of the living environment is the design of common spaces.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Once, my grassroots leader told me that he overheard two elderly ladies talking after an event.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: One of them was looking for a toilet and the other one said, "See, I told you to wear a diaper.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: My children bought me a few packs and I am using them.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: On one hand, I was amused and heartened by the lady's candour and outlook on life.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: She did not let her situation get in the way of her being active.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The point is that though there are some physical challenges when one gets older, challenges that robs you of your dignity, enthusiasm and interest in participating in activities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It is thus important that we continue to ensure that our living environment is made suitable to alleviate some of these challenges.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The proposal is, therefore, for the agencies to continue to look at the design of common spaces and take into account the challenges of the ageing population.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: For example, the agencies could ensure that there are more toilets and benches in parks near senior fitness corners or other common spaces so that we can improve the living environment for the elderly and encourage them to keep active.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I move to my third point on healthcare costs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I appreciate that much funds have been poured into this scheme.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I would have to though reflect the sentiments on the ground of the concerns regarding the regular medical costs that elderly residents have to incur.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I fully support the call to the Government and the community to continue strengthening the support for caregivers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In this regard, I would like to highlight the struggles of the sandwich class, who have to take care of both their elderly parents and their young children.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Often, in these families, the husband and wife are working and they rely on FDWs and childcare services.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I acknowledge and welcome the support for these families, like the working mother subsidies and relief and the FDW levy concessions.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The daily routine can already be rather draining, especially if the elderly need regular medical attention.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It gets more challenging when what I call the “expected unexpected event” takes place, such as when a child falls sick, the helper decides to go home, or a sudden project needs to be attended to at work.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: At times, all that can go wrong can go wrong at the same time.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: At this juncture, I would like to add that although the focus of this Motion is on the needs of the caregivers of the elderly, I hope that attention is also given to caregivers with children with special needs or persons with disabilities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: As a parent of a child with special needs, I can empathise with the challenges.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: For example, I have several residents who have more than one child with special needs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I know one parent who has three children with special needs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: She is a single mother and needs to work to sustain the family.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: She is not wealthy but appears to be managing well.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: One time, there was a change of helper and the new one was not able to handle her disabled children.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It was tough for her to manage work and the household during that period.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It is not easy to come up with a complete solution to support caregivers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: But one aspect we could look at is how we can work with employers to encourage FWAs in the office.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I appreciate that there are existing grants available but, perhaps, a more targeted push could be made to increase the adoption of the grant.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
