speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I gave the comparison to university faculty members on academic tenure, which is up to age 65, something that has been offered for about two decades in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I believe we can and should offer retirement only at age 65 across the board, especially when Singaporeans are living longer, marrying later, having children later, and would still need to earn a stable income even well into their 60s.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The offer for re-employment should then be from 66 to 70.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Companies and organisations also need to change their mindsets about having older employees continuing and still contributing at work.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As I have said before in this House, older Singaporean employees have a wealth of experience, wisdom as well as institutional and historical knowledge to share, particularly with their younger counterparts, and they should be valued for this.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Third, there needs to be in place sufficient policies to allow for meaningful employment of older Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While we can acknowledge that not many Singaporeans above the age of 60 can still carry on with physically demanding or laborious work, they can contribute in capacities, such as trainers, counselors, mentors and consultants.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Companies, organisations and our own public service sector need to explore how job redesign can be done to ensure older Singaporeans can continue to be gainfully employed with little or no "dumbing down" of their job scopes or work contribution.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: MOE is a good example of a public service employer of older Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Adjunct Teachers are employed even well into their 70s and they continue to contribute to the teaching of young students and the mentoring of younger teachers, without any "dumbing down" of their job scopes or work contribution.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope more of our public service Ministries and agencies can do the same as MOE when it comes to employing older Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Next, I wish to speak on caregivers for the elderly.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Once again, as our population ages, there will be more seniors and elderly Singaporeans who may need care in their golden years.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As we strive to help Singaporeans age actively, stay gainfully employed or remain relevant, there will be a group of elderly Singaporeans who need constant care as they lose the ability to care for themselves due to debilitating illnesses or age-related health conditions.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This group of Singaporeans will need caregivers to look after them on a 24/7 basis.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some will be able to employ foreign domestic helpers or professional caregivers, while others will end up getting the care they need in nursing homes.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, there are among us those who wish to take care of our elderly parents during their golden and most vulnerable years, out of a sense of filial piety.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This may not be an easy decision to make as there are opportunity costs involved, particularly in terms of income.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While there are some forms of caregiver support provided by the Government, there is room for this support to be enhanced.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These are about the only two forms of assistance for caregivers of elderly Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I believe the caregivers among us need more support as they care for their elderly parents.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would urge the Government to look into providing more financial support to the caregivers among us who have decided to care for their elderly parents beyond the CTG or IDAPE.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: More importantly, I hope that, as a society, we will accord greater respect towards those who choose careers in gerontology, geriatrics and elderly caregiving because, beyond just a career, they have chosen to provide care and support towards our elders.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, there are still areas in which we can strengthen our policies and initiatives to ensure older Singaporeans remain active, relevant and gainfully employed, our elderly are able to get the care they need, and our caregivers for the elderly can also get the support that would make their choice to care a lot easier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In particular, Members have spoken about the need for a whole-of-society effort to help seniors age with purpose and with dignity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Members have also affirmed the critical role that caregivers play in achieving this, so that our seniors can better age in place and, as far as possible, in the company and care of those who love them the most.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I agree, and the Government intends to introduce measures to help caregivers on their journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As our population ages and more Singaporeans live longer, we will see a rise in informal caregiving.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As Dr Chia Shi-Lu noted in his speech at the outset, Singaporeans will need support in caring for their loved ones, and working caregivers will need to balance employment and their family responsibilities as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I am mindful that there is a broad range of different caregivers, and we have heard different stories from different perspectives, all of which are very relevant to the debate today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There is a broad range of these different caregivers who operate in a variety of different circumstances and in a very broad landscape and they also themselves wear multiple hats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Some may care for different groups of care recipients, such as seniors or children or, as Ms Denise Phua mentioned, PWDs, or any combination of this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Their needs are diverse, as with their own particular family or caregiving circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, over time, we will need to look carefully at what these needs are and whether further assistance might be needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As a start and particularly given our demographic shift over the next decade which I have outlined above, I will focus on how we can support senior caregivers as vital partners in our health and social system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Some of the measures that I will outline will also apply to other groups of caregivers, for example, those looking after PWDs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And my colleague, Minister of State Sam Tan will touch more on this when he speaks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As Mr Murali Pillai and Dr Lily Neo noted, many caregivers naturally prefer for their loved ones to age-in-place at home, in familiar surroundings and in the company of people they know and love.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We agree entirely, and it really goes without saying.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As such, the Government has been taking the lead to anchor care in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Over the years, MOH has strengthened the broad ecosystem of support for senior caregiving by expanding the capacity of aged care services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have also deepened the range of care options available for our seniors, through new models, such as the Integrated Home and Day Care programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are encouraged to see a higher take-up of home and community care services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ultimately, for whatever additional hardware that we put in place, it is the people talent that is the most important, and we agree with both Ms Anthea Ong and Mr Melvin Yong that healthcare professionals play a key role in providing quality aged care services for our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Between 2012 and 2017, MOH had provided funding support to raise the wages of workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Salaries of workers across participating providers saw a 30% increase in aggregate over this period of time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MOH also supports skills training scholarships and grants, and productivity improvement and job redesign initiatives to raise the value of jobs, alongside salary increases in line with the intent of the Progressive Wage Model (PWM).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will continue to work with employers to review salaries of workers regularly to ensure that they are adequately recognised for their efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MOH will study if further efforts are needed, including whether to introduce a PWM for the eldercare sector with the tripartite partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have also put in place long-term care financing measures to ensure affordable and also sustainable healthcare.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Today, we see means-tested subsidies for aged care services, which is complemented by our long-term insurance care schemes like ElderShield and CareShield Life, and a range of disability schemes, such as IDAPE, which Ms Intan Mokhtar has mentioned, and the Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme (Pioneer-DAS).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For those who still have difficulty paying for care after Government subsidies, grants and insurance scheme payouts  notwithstanding these programmes, there are also Government-funded safety nets, such as MediFund and ComCare, which can provide further assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At the same time, we will also take the opportunity to review the household income criteria for other healthcare subsidy schemes as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Taken together, these efforts support ageing in place, living with purpose and dignity, and also provide caregivers with peace of mind.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But we can still do more to directly address the needs of caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In the various engagements that we have had with caregivers since September last year, many shared with us the challenges they face in caring for their loved ones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Whilst they face challenges, they also left us in no doubt how the caregiving journey is itself a very rewarding process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: That is also the sentiment that many Members here today have expressed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: No two caregivers' journeys would be similar, but each of these experiences is bound by the same common desire to care for, and give the best to, their care recipient.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This action plan outlines key initiatives that we will embark on in the next two years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There are five broad themes which underpin our action plan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They are, firstly, Care Navigation; secondly, Financial Support; thirdly, Workplace Support; fourth, Caregiver Respite Services; and finally, Caregiver Empowerment and Training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As mentioned by Dr Chia Shi-Lu, many caregivers, particularly the new ones, the new caregivers, need ready access to information and referral to services, but they may not know so well where to turn to, how to navigate the landscape, whom to turn to for help, and whom to consult in their time of need, particularly the new ones who may suddenly and very quickly embark on this caregiving responsibility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Today, we have physical touchpoints – AICare Links, operated by AIC in acute and community hospitals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The AIC Office at Maxwell Road caters to walk-ins from caregivers and seniors alike, and provides information and assistance regarding eldercare services, grants and schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The public can also, of course, obtain information through AIC’s helpline, the Singapore Silver Line.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These are all useful but perhaps not enough.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We need to do more to help caregivers feel supported and confident in making informed decisions regarding the caregiving needs of their loved ones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We agree with Dr Lily Neo that we need to synergise our efforts with SSOs and other Government touchpoints within the community to make service delivery more cohesive and unified which, overall, will then better serve the needs of seniors and caregivers alike in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui highlighted earlier the need to look out for elderly caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We agree and, through our Community Networks for Seniors initiative, Silver Generation Ambassadors will identify these elderly caregivers during home visits and link them up with services and support schemes relevant to their particular circumstances and needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As Mr Melvin Yong also noted, technology is fast becoming a key enabler in providing caregivers with useful information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The web portal on eldercare and caregiving, Singapore Silver Pages, will be revamped this year to improve the overall user experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will also develop a Health Marketplace e-platform by 2020, where users can more directly access services, such as Medical Escort and Transport, and also purchase regular consumables.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For such services, it helps that a caregiver has the option of not having to make a trip to a physical office or speak to someone over the phone, just in order to access those services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As part of our Smart Nation efforts, MOH has been working with GovTech and other Government agencies on a cross-agency Moments of Life Digital Portal to aid Singaporeans, including caregivers, with pre-planning for the end-of-life journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Features will include step-by-step guidance on issues, such as Advance Care Planning, making wills and settling post-death estate matters as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will roll out the beta version by the end of 2019 and will work with the relevant touchpoints to raise awareness of these pre-planning tools.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Next, let me turn to improving financial support for caregiving needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Several Members, including Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Christopher de Souza, Dr Intan Mokhtar and Mr Chen Show Mao have suggested providing further financial support to manage caregiving expenses, especially for those being cared for at home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: From our engagement sessions, many caregivers have, indeed, shared with us that the cost of caregiving is amongst the uppermost issues on their minds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Currently, we already have several schemes in place to support ageing in place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These include the Seniors’ Mobility and Enabling Fund to defray the cost of assistive devices and home healthcare items, the FDW Grant to offset the costs of hiring an FDW, as well as the CTG to subsidise training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will build on these to boost support for caregiving in home and community settings, so as to achieve, amongst others, a delay or even a reduction in the need for institutional care for our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: HCG will be means-tested and available to care recipients with permanent moderate disability, regardless of age and granted on criteria which are similar to what we now use for the FDW grant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: HCG can be used to offset the costs of long-term caregiving in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: HCG will complement severe disability schemes like ElderShield and CareShield Life, by providing support earlier, and at a stage when care recipients are still able to perform these ADLs, albeit with some assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In other words, HCG will be available at an earlier and less severe stage of disability, when compared to the criteria in disability schemes, such as ElderShield or CareShield Life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I have earlier said that no two caregivers' journey is similar.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Indeed, there are very many differences in the journey and also the way in which care is expected to be delivered.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have noted Mr Christopher de Souza and Ms Tin Pei Ling's point that care arrangements may vary from person to person or, indeed, may even vary depending on which stage of care the recipient might be in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We want to be able to provide financial support which will better meet the range of diverse caregiving needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At present, the current FDW Grant can only be used to offset the cost of hiring an FDW.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Some might use it to help with the cost of hiring an FDW, if that is what is needed, whilst others could choose to use this sum to defray the cost of caregiving expenses, such as the costs for home and community-based services, and transportation to medical appointments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There is much greater flexibility in how this grant can be used.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Care recipients who qualify can choose to nominate their caregiver to receive HCG.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms Joan Pereira has also suggested that we broaden the definition of family members in Government policies to strengthen familial support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These measures will complement our existing suite of long-term care financing measures supporting family caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, they come on top of those measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Next, more and more families face a growing caregiving burden but also coupled with their own work commitments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, the workplace environment is a key consideration as we chart this landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Employers also have to play a part in creating supportive workplaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Caregiving leave has been mooted by several Members in this House here today and also before this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: While we acknowledge that there are merits to extending leave provisions, we also need a sustainable approach that balances the needs of not just employees but also employers in the long term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This was a point which was widely discussed at the various consultations we had with caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As Dr Chia Shi-Lu noted, many caregivers see FWAs as being more useful to helping them meet both their work and caregiving commitments and balancing them in the longer term in a more sustainable way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For example, working caregivers would like the flexibility to be able to take time-off to tend to their loved ones’ needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Often, they do not need a full day or even half a day and, perhaps two to three hours might be sufficient in some circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Other caregivers may require flexibility to work offsite on occasion whilst they take care of their dependants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In our view, a better and more sustainable long-term approach to this issue would be for employers and companies to develop their own FWAs which can best support caregivers in the workplace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In addition to FWAs, as Mr Melvin Yong noted, some caregivers wish to re-enter the workforce and need more support as well, such as in upskilling and job seeking.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: My colleague, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Low Yen Ling will be sharing more details of our recommendations to support these groups in her speech later.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I turn now to the point made by various Members on the importance of caregivers being able to take occasional breaks during their journeys to rest, recharge and, sometimes, to deal with their own particular circumstances as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Sometimes, a respite is not even a luxury because some caregivers might require the respite at short notice due to their own exigencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They cannot always anticipate when they might themselves fall ill, or when they might have an urgent matter to deal with.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: How they are going to be able to take some time off to tend to these exigencies while at the same time ensuring that their loved ones remain cared for remains a significant burden.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Respite services within home and institutional settings are already presently available.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But again, we can do more, and MOH will be enhancing our suite of respite options so that more caregivers can benefit from respite services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We also want to ensure that caregivers can access such services in a shorter period of time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For instance, we have heard from caregivers that seniors with dementia can sometimes have difficulty sleeping and resting at night.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In fact, some of these seniors with dementia can be quite active at night.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling shared about caregivers who find it challenging as their own sleep then becomes disrupted when they need to tend to the seniors at night, especially if they also have to juggle work commitments in the morning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: AIC will partner a few nursing home providers to provide this new option where seniors with dementia can be engaged through activities at night while their caregivers can catch up on their own rest.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As I mentioned earlier, the need for respite services can be unpredictable and we need to be able to cater for caregivers getting respite quickly and efficiently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Under such a system, caregivers can pre-register their loved ones and complete some of the otherwise lengthy and somewhat laborious administrative processes upfront.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Later on, when the time comes for the respite services to be availed of, providers would already have some of the key information, and this would help to cut down the administrative process and time required to enrol the senior.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Caregivers of terminally ill patients are fulfilling the desires of their loved ones by caring for them and also enabling them to pass on at home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The pilot would provide custodial care service for home palliative care patients so that caregivers can take a break with the knowledge that their loved ones will still be well taken care of at home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Next, let me touch on caregiver empowerment and training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As members have noted, beyond just having a strong suite of formal services to support caregivers, good socio-emotional support for caregivers is also crucial.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We already have community outreach teams who currently reach out to those at risk or those with mental health illnesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will evolve some of these teams to provide a more dedicated focus on caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These teams will provide outreach to caregivers, provide case management and support through counselling, and also offer socio-emotional programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will also facilitate more caregiver support networks being set up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Caregiver support networks provide a safe environment for caregivers to come together, share their caregiving experience, lean on one another, support one another, which is often needed during the long and oftentimes difficult caregiving journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Take the example of Mdm Theresa Toh who cares for her 68-year-old sister with schizophrenia and attends Queenstown Caregiver Connect, a support group for caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Queenstown Caregiver Connect helps Mdm Toh with self-care by organising talks on mindfulness and communications with her loved ones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: She has also, through this programme, met with fellow caregivers with whom she has now a strong friendship and there is a group to lean on and someone with whom she can empathise with.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We plan to expand more of such caregiver support networks through our Dementia Friendly Communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms Anthea Ong noted that it is critical to equip our caregivers with the right skills and the relevant knowledge through training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Many households rely on FDWs to support their caregiving needs and we want to equip them with the relevant caregiving skills upstream so that they can take better care of our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: On this note, I am very encouraged to hear about the several community and ground-up initiatives to recognise and support our caregivers mentioned by Members, such as Mr Murali Pillai and Er Dr Lee Bee Wah as well, to build a support structure to reach out, to empathise with and help caregivers on this journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We would agree that everyone in society has a part to play in this caregiving journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I have heard many Members expressed that sentiment and I agree entirely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For instance, the Caregiver Alliance Limited partnered the Chinatown Heritage Centre and Nanyang Polytechnic (NYP) this year to organise an event for caregivers and their loved ones at the Centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Caregivers had the opportunity to network and share experiences while nursing students from NYP role-played characters from the past and conducted therapeutic and fun activities to engage the young and old alike, including baking, childhood games and paper art.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will continue to work closely with community partners, such as Community Development Councils and grassroots organisations, to strengthen community-level support for caregivers, as Mr Murali Pillai has suggested.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In response also to Mr Mohamed Irshad's suggestion to more systematically track caregivers, our various initiatives will give us the opportunity to collect more comprehensive information on caregivers to better understand their profile and needs and what else could be done to enhance the support given to them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They do not complain and they are often determined and resilient in overcoming the challenges that come their way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Caregiving journeys may be long, but we can go the distance if families and communities come together to support the caregivers in our midst.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is not just about grants, hardware or programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is also about appreciation and empathy and, in the words of Ms Anthea Ong, about embracing caregiving as a society to ensure that we not just provide the physical and hardware support but also the socio-emotional support that we owe caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is about nurturing the kind of society we want to foster.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Action Plan reflects the Government's commitment to strengthen support for senior caregiving and our call for a whole-of-society effort to partner caregivers in their caregiving journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Each of us must do our part to recognise, value, support and celebrate caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: On this note, Mr Speaker, I support the Motion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Japan has already started challenging the notion of what "old" means.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Japan Gerontological Society shared a report in 2017 which recognised how their current seniors are much fitter than past generations, and suggested redefining "old" as those “over 75".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We can redefine ageing and turn it into a positive force if we embrace longevity and its opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have made good progress on these initiatives, including on senior-friendly designs, as raised by Ms Tin Pei Ling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As we continue to make progress on these initiatives, we need to plan ahead for successive generations of seniors who have different needs and aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Merdeka Generation seniors, for example, are living longer and healthier and are more educated, skilled and IT-savvy, compared to our Pioneers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: MOH is strengthening efforts in three areas to enable Singaporeans to look forward to their senior years with confidence and grace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We call it the "3Es" framework – one, Empowering good health and active ageing; two, Enabling communities of care; and three, Evolving new models of ageing in place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: First, we want to empower seniors to stay healthy and active and provide opportunities for personal development and community participation so that they can continue to find purpose and meaning in their senior years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Good health is a life asset that we must continue to invest in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have expanded the reach of preventive health services to seniors in the community in recent years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Last year, we rolled out Project Silver Screen, in partnership with Temasek Foundation Cares, to check seniors' vision, hearing and oral health, at low or no cost, and follow-up on abnormal results if needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are also leveraging our network of about 3,000 Silver Generation (SG) Ambassadors to proactively assess seniors' health status when they visit them at home and encourage them to participate in the preventive health and active ageing programmes in their neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As noted by Dr Lily Neo, we are also extending active ageing programmes to more communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: By 2020, two in three RCs nationwide will host active ageing programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We agree with Mr Darryl David that efforts to inculcate healthy living habits among seniors should start early.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: One of the ways we do this is by targeting mature workers aged 40 and above through HPB's workplace health programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Over 60,000 mature workers in seven sectors, including transport and security, have participated in such programmes which have been customised to each sector’s workplace environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In line with his suggestion for a multi-agency approach, we formed the HealthySG Taskforce in November last year to coordinate an integrated approach across public agencies to encourage Singaporeans to adopt a healthy lifestyle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The taskforce, chaired by Senior Parliamentary Secretary Amrin Amin, is in the process of gathering feedback and ideas and we look forward to the public’s contributions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Ms Joan Pereira and Dr Lily Neo suggested building more SACs to promote wellness activities close to where seniors live.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Besides SACs, we have also been siting such programmes in eldercare facilities to provide a continuum of active ageing and care services to seniors in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: One example, as shared by Ms Joan Pereira, is the “Wellness Kampung” initiative in Yishun.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Piloted in 2016 as a partnership between Yishun Health, St Luke's ElderCare and the Nee Soon grassroots organisations, the network of three wellness and care centres provide wellness activities, such as healthy cooking demonstrations and recreational activities, as well as day care and rehabilitation services for frail seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: MOH is also building larger day care centres called "Active Ageing Hubs" which offer a range of active ageing and care services, similar to the "Wellness Kampung".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have opened five such hubs to date and expect another five by 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Going forward, we will work closely with community partners to provide a good range of customised active ageing programmes to suit different profiles of seniors in their neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: While the gender diversity debate in the corporate world has been cast as a shortage of women directors in listed and non-listed companies, it is interesting that the problem is reversed for our seniors in these programmes – men are scarce in this space!

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Anecdotally, our community partners share the same observation as Mr Ang Wei Neng that only about one in five or 20% of their participants are men.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Even for senior learning courses, only about 30% of the participants are men.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We agree with Mr Ang Wei Neng that there is scope to increase male participation in our active ageing programmes and are determined to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The example he shared of the Men's Shed movement in Australia is interesting, as it recognises that men find it easier to make friends through work-based activities, such as carpentry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We may not have backyards or sheds like in Australia, but we have our void decks and common spaces, where we can see our men at work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For example, in Kampung Senang, male senior volunteers under the "Silver Mobility Aiders" programme help to maintain and service wheelchairs for their fellow seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In Yishun, the "Repair Kakis", a group made up of about 15 men who used to be technicians, electricians and engineers, get together weekly to help repair, assemble and fix various electrical appliances brought in by their fellow residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I am encouraged to hear that Mr Henry Kwek is planning to bring in more communal sports for the senior men in Kebun Baru.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Indeed, we need a concerted effort to find meaningful activities and innovative ways to bring the male seniors together and create local versions of these men's sheds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For a start, MOH welcomes suggestions from all the men in this House on new active ageing approaches to get men not just to talk, but also to learn and play "shoulder to shoulder".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We also want to support our seniors' aspirations to continue learning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will continue to grow the senior learning opportunities under the NSA, including in areas, such as IT and digital literacy, as suggested by Ms Joan Pereira and Ms Tin Pei Ling, and make them even more accessible by bringing more of these courses into the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Seniors can also utilise their SkillsFuture Credits for many of the NSA courses to learn new skills that can help them find freelance work opportunities, as suggested by Mr Henry Kwek.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We recognise that seniors are invaluable assets to the community, and we want to empower them to contribute their knowledge and wisdom by volunteering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: One example is 68-year-old Mr Chia Shih Thow who started volunteering with Montfort Care 10 years ago after he attended their Young At Heart (YAH!) programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Chia was inspired to hear of other senior volunteers through the programme and signed up as a Health Ambassador first, before taking on other roles, such as medical escort, befriender and games facilitator.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: He is now back at where he discovered his passion for volunteering, inspiring others as a group facilitator in the YAH! programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To help others like Mr Chia give back to the community, we have set up the Silver Volunteer Fund (SVF) to provide funding by community-based organisations that create volunteering opportunities for our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have other sources of funding to support good ground-up initiatives, such as the Tote Board Community Healthcare Fund (TBCHF) and the Community Silver Trust (CST) dollar-for-dollar matching grant which was extended to active ageing programmes in 2017.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will continue to review the funding for such programmes, including the suggestion by Dr Teo Ho Pin to set up a Healthy Living Endowment fund.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Second, we want to enable strong and cohesive networks of care that support all seniors, especially vulnerable seniors, to age in place with dignity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Senior Minister of State Edwin Tong has talked about how we can strengthen support for family caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The community plays a key role in supplementing and complementing the care and support provided by families to build a robust community care ecosystem for our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We envision such an ecosystem to be underpinned by four key layers of support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: First, through the "preventive health home visits" which I talked about earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Second, by providing a systematic and comprehensive range of preventive health and active ageing programmes, such as chronic disease screening and nutrition classes, in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Third, building up a network of befrienders in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: And fourth, linking them up with the necessary care and support services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Henry Kwek talked about the importance of local coordination.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We agree with Miss Cheng Li Hui that more support should be extended to vulnerable seniors who are at high risk of social isolation and loneliness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Faisal Manap also raised the issue of elderly suicide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To clarify, while the number of elderly suicides has increased in recent years, along with our ageing population, the suicide death rates among our elderly have, in fact, declined over the past decade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Hence, we will further strengthen our efforts to prevent suicides by proactively reaching out to pre-empt social isolation and provide support for those at risk.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For example, our SG Ambassadors today are trained to identify seniors at risk of social isolation when they make their home visits and will proactively link them up to community befrienders in their neighbourhood who can check in on them regularly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Care Line, a 24-hour senior helpline, which will be expanded nationwide, also calls seniors regularly to check whether they are well and provides urgent assistance if seniors call in, distressed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our community outreach teams managed by community service providers also reach out to seniors with or at-risk of dementia and depression.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah shared examples of how the senior residents in her constituency help other seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Indeed, seniors find it easier to relate to and befriend other seniors, for example, by being able to communicate in their native dialect and mother tongue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: They are a valuable volunteer resource pool to tap on, as highlighted by Ms Joan Pereira.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Building communities of care involves our younger generation as well, and I am heartened to hear of the intergenerational initiatives shared by Mr Mohamed Irshad.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Council for Third Age (C3A) organises intergenerational learning programmes which provide opportunities for seniors and students to interact and learn from each other.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Under the Action Plan for Successful Ageing, we are also co-locating childcare and eldercare facilities, such as those in Mr Christopher de Souza's ward, to facilitate intergenerational programming.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Third, we want to continue to evolve our typologies of ageing in place to meet the needs and aspirations of future generations of seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In recent years, the Government has announced efforts to ensure that our current and upcoming cohorts of seniors, such as the Merdeka Generation, have greater assurance for issues of concern to them, such as coping with healthcare expenses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: More details on the Merdeka Generation Package will be shared at Budget.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I will also share more about how we will reach out to the Merdeka Generation seniors at the Committee of Supply this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We need to anticipate what future generations of seniors might deem important to age in place gracefully and confidently, and be prepared to evolve our models of care, or experiment with new ones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Melvin Yong has suggested a review of the current Build-Own-Lease (BOL) funding model for nursing homes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We do regularly review our nursing home development costs and nursing home development models.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our BOL framework introduced in 2012 has allowed us to ramp up our nursing home capacity to meet the needs of our frail seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Under this framework, the Government pays for the capital costs of development and tenders out the operating rights to both private and VWO operators so that these operators do not have to bear the upfront capital costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This model also allowed us to encourage quality care as providers are evaluated on the quality of their proposals, which includes aspects like model of care and community integration plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our tenders allow providers to propose how much they intend to charge patients based on what is sustainable to them, and the price competition helps keep nursing home fees affordable for elderly residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We also regularly review our funding for nursing homes, separately from the providers' fee bids, to ensure providers are adequately funded for the services provided to subsidised residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will continue to review our BOL framework to ensure that nursing home residents can access good and appropriate care at affordable fees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We continue to find innovative ways to mobilise community resources to better support our seniors, such as in the area of transport raised by Miss Cheryl Chan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: AIC had worked with private-hire companies, such as Grab, to train their drivers to help seniors who have limited mobility or are in wheelchairs, get into or out of the car safely to bring them to their medical appointments or to senior centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The GrabAssist service is also available for those who wish to book a ride from the over 1,000 drivers that have been trained to date.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Another area we are looking to evolve new typologies of ageing in place is in the staging of assisted living (AL) services within housing estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In 2014, we piloted "in situ" care precincts by staging care services and AL support out of SACs within rental precincts through our Care Close to Home (C2H) programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are reviewing how we can develop new options of AL for seniors to facilitate ageing in place, as suggested also by Mr Henry Kwek, Ms Joan Pereira and Ms Rahayu Mahzam.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As announced at the Committee of Supply last year, MOH is working closely with MND to develop new AL options that include care services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: More details will be shared at the Committee of Supply this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Longevity is not a curse but a blessing and offers us possibilities to live more meaningful and productive lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As future cohorts of seniors are more educated and skilled, there is no better time to take advantage of our longer life years than now.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I personally believe that there is no better investment to make than that in good health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As the Chinese saying goes, "Health is Wealth" or "健康是财富".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Just as the Pioneer and Merdeka Generations have each played key roles in shaping Singapore's early years, we all have a responsibility today to shape our communities to build successive generations of successful agers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: On this note, Mr Speaker, I support both Motions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: As shared by a few Members earlier, it is not uncommon to find caregivers neglecting their own well-being, or suffering from burnout, when taking care of their dependants.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This is why "Supporting Caregivers" is a key thrust of our Third Enabling Masterplan (EMP3).

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Through EMP3, we want to help caregivers provide the best possible care to their loved ones, and also to take care of themselves.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Caregivers of adults with special needs and caregivers of seniors actually face similar challenges, such as physical care tasks, care affordability, accessing information and maintaining their emotional well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Allow me to highlight how caregivers of persons with special needs will benefit from the Caregiver Action Plan.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: For example, it can be used to pay for out-of-pocket expenses, such as Day Activity Centre fees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: MOM is also encouraging more employers to incorporate FWAs to reduce stress faced by working caregivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: FWAs give working caregivers greater flexibility to manage their time when the caregiving need arises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Beyond the caregiver action plans, MSF and our partners also support caregivers through various initiatives targeted at helping caregivers across life stages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Allow me to share some of these examples.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We are improving support for caregivers and parents of children with developmental needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Earlier this year, MSF announced that we will make Early Intervention services more customised to the developmental needs of children and also make them more affordable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Children under two will receive intervention under a new Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children (EIPIC) Under-2s programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This programme focuses on training parents and caregivers to include intervention strategies in the child's daily routines in their own home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We will also increase subsidies so that early intervention services are made more affordable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Taking care of persons with special needs is a lifelong journey and, for some, a lifelong commitment, and the support and guidance from other caregivers play an important part in helping them overcome difficult times.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: For this purpose, SG Enable has been working with the community to facilitate peer-to-peer training to equip caregivers with the skills to mentor and guide other caregivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Last December, Minister Desmond Lee launched the Caregivers Pod at Enabling Village.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This is a space specifically set aside for caregivers to take part in peer support activities and caregiver training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Beyond being a place for caregivers to meet, the Caregivers Pod is also a platform for them to connect and share experiences and expertise and strengthen peer support among themselves.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Connecting caregivers, whether physically, or even through mobile chat groups, allows them to seek advice or share their own experiences with others, including the Government and service providers, more effectively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: For example, after meeting Minister Desmond Lee at the Caregivers Pod last year, a group of 15 caregivers came together and proposed a list of priorities that are most needed by caregivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: So, we welcome such ground-up initiatives and we are looking into how we can work together with them to address their concerns through customised solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We are also aware that caregivers, especially older caregivers, worry about care arrangements for their children with special needs after they themselves have passed on.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We also set up the Special Needs Saving Scheme in 2012 to enable parents to set aside CPF for the long-term care of their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We will continue to explore more avenues and schemes to help address such concerns.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: MSF is constantly looking at how we can improve the services we offer to caregivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: I, therefore, thank the Members for sharing with us their accounts of the struggles that caregivers in their constituencies face in seeking assistance from the Government.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Indeed, as pointed out by Ms Denise Phua, these are complex cases for which there are no one-size-fits-all solutions or, in her words, cookie-cutter policies, to address each individual issue.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: While the Government must do better to ensure that caregivers in need of help do not fall through the gaps, I thank Ms Denise Phua for also recognising that the Government alone cannot resolve all the issues, and that we need to involve the wider community to support the needy in our midst.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: That said, MSF plans to strengthen case coordination and management to provide better social assistance in cases of complex needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We will share more about these plans at the Committee of Supply this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: For example, the EMP3 steering committee called for improved access to information on disability-related social support and services and suggested creating a one-stop information portal for caregivers to meet their needs for information on services, caregiving, self-care and well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: To answer this call, SG Enable is developing a new online portal that will act as a 24/7 information hub pointing caregivers to social support available for their care recipients and also for themselves.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Parents know that they will not always be able to take care of their children, and they hope that their children will be able to find and hold on to good jobs and live independently despite their special needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We understand all these hopes and concerns and want to assure them that MSF is committed to meeting the employment needs and enhancing the independent living prospects of persons with special needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Our "Future Economy" and "Smart Nation" drive will not leave their children behind, but rather, be enablers for greater inclusion both in the workforce and also in the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: As part of our efforts to engage the community to co-design and co-create solutions, we are examining these issues together with persons with special needs, their caregivers, Government agencies, VWOs and other stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: MSF will elaborate on all these plans at the Committee of Supply.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Now, let me touch on the topic of helping more Singaporeans make a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) which some Members, including Miss Cheryl Chan, have raised.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The chances of losing mental capacity increase as we age.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: As individuals, we can plan early to appoint a family member to make decisions for us when we lose mental capacity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This advance planning will give our caregivers clarity and peace of mind.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Making an LPA is, therefore, very critical, and MSF will continue to encourage more Singaporeans to do so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: To raise awareness, we recently launched a radio campaign in January to encourage more Singaporeans to make an LPA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We have also partnered other agencies to hold public education talks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: For example, we worked with HDB to inform Singaporeans on LPAs at HDB's series of Heartland Talks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We will continue with these public education efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In closing, Sir, I thank my MOH colleagues for putting together the Caregiver Action Plan, as well as the caregivers and community partners who stepped forward to provide feedback during the consultations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The plans are an important step in the right direction, as pointed out by Members of this House.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: I believe that, together with the support and partnership of the people, private and public sectors, we can build a more inclusive society for all.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It is not surprising that housing and the design of our urban environment is close to the hearts of many, given that it affects the daily lived experiences of all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam spoke about how we could build more facilities, such as toilets and benches, near to senior fitness corners and parks to encourage seniors to exercise more frequently.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our parks are enjoyed by families, groups of friends and Singaporeans of all ages.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: All of them have benches and resting spots which seniors may use.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In addition, toilets and shelters have been installed in our bigger and more frequented parks, such as our national gardens, regional parks and nature parks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The National Parks Board (NParks) has been upgrading our green spaces to encourage seniors to age not only actively, but also comfortably and safely.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These efforts include incorporating new senior-friendly amenities, such as fitness corners, shelters, toilets and footpaths; replacing metal drain covers next to footpaths to minimise the risk of seniors tripping and falling over; and also improving the lighting in parks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: NParks has made good progress on these initiatives and will continue to enhance efforts in this area.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to review the provision of senior-friendly facilities in our parks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Apart from parks, we agree with Dr Lily Neo and Ms Tin Pei Ling that it is important to consciously design our housing estates and buildings to be senior-friendly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Since 2006, all new HDB estates have incorporated Universal Design features, for instance, building common spaces with ramps instead of steps, having barrier-free routes to connect various amenities, having more seating in common spaces, and mounting letter boxes at comfortable heights.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Within the flats, lever door handles and rocker switches are mounted at lower heights, and we have widened corridors and doorways to allow for better wheelchair manoeuvrability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our short-lease 2-room flexi flats, which are meant for seniors, also come fitted upfront with grab bars.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Under the Optional Component Scheme, seniors may choose to have their flats come complete with a wardrobe, kitchen hobs and cabinets.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These come with elderly-friendly features, such as lower clothes hanging rods for easy reach, and wheels on the bottom of kitchen cabinets so that they may be rearranged easily.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In addition, seniors can opt for lower kitchen countertops and cabinets, especially for wheelchair users.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These homes will be equipped with additional infrastructure, such as additional power and data points, to support the easy installation of smart systems within the flat.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We expect these flats to be completed next year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For existing blocks, Members will also be familiar with the various upgrading programmes in your respective neighbourhoods, such as Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE) which provides senior-friendly features.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Members are also welcome to play a role in adapting the estate to the needs of elderly residents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For instance, Town Councils can add more benches and ramps by tapping on our various upgrading programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While HDB communal areas are typically not provisioned with toilets as they are located near the residents' homes, neighbourhood centres or eating establishments so that seniors can have ready access to toilet facilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Nonetheless, should there be demand for public toilets at specific locations in selected precincts where there is an ongoing Neighbourhood Renewal Programme (NRP), Members can highlight the request under the NRP.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: HDB will assess these requests on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Dr Teo Ho Pin raised the issue of funding caps for CIPC projects.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While there are caps in place for items on the CIPC menu, these are meant to ensure prudent use of Government monies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Nonetheless, we can assess requests on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Beyond just housing estates, we also carefully consider how buildings can be thoughtfully designed to cater to all elderly users and workers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We agree with Mr Zainal Sapari that it is important to provide adequate rest areas for our elderly workers and we will work with the other agencies to look into the Member's suggestions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Joan Pereira suggested building more blocks of integrated housing, similar to Kampung Admiralty.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In Kampung Admiralty, HDB advanced the concept of being senior-friendly by building a whole development with senior residents in mind, and integrating their housing with healthcare, wellness and eldercare facilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They also included a childcare centre, shops and eateries that bring the different generations together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It is, as the Prime Minister said in the National Day message last year, a "high-rise kampung where residents are out and about, socialising with family, friends and neighbours, and yet never too far from home".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will look to do more of such integrated developments, where there are suitable sites.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: However, not all seniors may wish to move out of their current residence, as many may prefer to age in place.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Therefore, the Government's strategy is also to retrofit existing HDB estates to make them senior-friendly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will make sure that there is a good range of socio-communal facilities, such as eldercare and childcare centres, so that our seniors have good access to the provision of various services, wherever they may be staying.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Members have also suggested having Group Homes and AL services for seniors in our public housing, which Senior Minister of State Amy Khor has responded to.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will share more details at the upcoming Committee of Supply debate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
