text: As for the private sector, MND, MOH and URA agree with Ms Rahayu Mahzam that there is an increasing need for more diverse housing options for seniors, particularly those that twin housing and care services, to better allow able seniors to meaningfully age in place.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Agencies have been working with them to study and facilitate suitable retirement housing typologies in the private market that will work for our local context.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will share more details in due course.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It is also important that the private sector also study the provision of AL services to cater to this segment, so that Retirement Housing products can be more meaningful and attractive for seniors in the long term.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These findings will help shape and regulate the development of the private retirement housing market going forward.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Henry Kwek also touched on how we could facilitate and strengthen family support for our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MND recognises the role that housing can play in encouraging mutual care and support among family members, whether it is through introducing flat typologies that are suitable for multi-generational living, such as our 3-Generation (3Gen) flats; or helping families to live together or close to one another, through our various grants and schemes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For instance, priority schemes, such as the Married Child Priority Scheme (MCPS), the Multi-Generational Priority Scheme and the Senior Priority Scheme, which give flat buyers priority when applying for a new flat with HDB with or near their parents or married children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Over the years, our public rental flats have played an important role in helping our most vulnerable seniors who face difficulties in securing a roof over their heads.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Singles currently apply for public rental under the Joint Singles Scheme and share a flat.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan suggested allowing those with health conditions to live alone.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For those with medical conditions that make it difficult to flat-share, HDB already allows them to rent alone if they have a doctor's recommendation to do so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Separately, since 2015, HDB has made available some new 1-room rental flats with partitions to create separate sleeping areas for each occupant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will explore how to make more partitioned flats available to Joint Singles.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan also suggested further finetuning the criteria for other groups who may need rental flats.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For seniors with serious illnesses who monetised their homes to fund their treatment, HDB considers their medical conditions and expenses if they appeal for public rental, and exercises flexibility based on their individual circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Seniors whose family relations have broken down but still own a flat can seek help from Family Service Centres, which would facilitate family reconciliation and coordinate support for the seniors’ other needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is important as the senior still has rights to his or her property.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: If the senior is in urgent housing need in the interim, MSF and HDB will work together to provide accommodation for the senior.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam also spoke about having more flexibility and compassion in assessing applicants' eligibility for various schemes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As the Member has noted, we do exercise flexibility based on the circumstance of each case.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But we will be happy to engage the Member on this specific case and assist the resident where needed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We agree that more can be done to provide flexibility for buyers of shorter lease flats, while still safeguarding their retirement adequacy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are working with CPF Board to review and update the CPF rules for the purchase of older flats and will announce them once the details are ready.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan also spoke about seniors having to top up their RA in order to qualify for LBS.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The LBS allows seniors to monetise their flat for their retirement needs while continuing to live in it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As such, the LBS proceeds are, first, used to meet the members' CPF retirement needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This ensures that seniors are able to benefit from a lifelong income stream under CPF LIFE.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Any remaining amount can then be taken out in cash.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will be looking forward to share more details of our plans at the upcoming Committee of Supply debates.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On this note, Mr Speaker, I support both Motions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: A year ago, this House discussed a Motion on Support for Senior Citizens, which called on the Government to spearhead community efforts and strengthen support for seniors to thrive and age with dignity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The two Motions today continue to uphold the spirit of last year's Motion and underscore the importance of supporting older Singaporeans' work aspirations and also their role as caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our nation's fast-ageing population, longer life expectancy and low birth rates are recasting the roles that older workers will play in our economy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In the last one year, I have spoken to many employers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many employers are looking at how older workers can be a crucial solution to their manpower needs, and our seniors are rising to the challenge.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We are already seeing this bear out in our employment numbers and trends.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This ranks us 11th, compared to other OECD countries, above the UK, Australia and the US.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Supporting and empowering older workers continue to be our key priority.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The rise in older worker employment has come about due to the close partnership and efforts of the tripartite partners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many Members spoke about the tripartite partners working together to raise the retirement and re-employment age.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This was done through careful deliberations over the years and is part of the "whole-of-Singapore effort" to address our demographic challenges.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Dr Intan Mokhtar asked to raise the retirement and re-employment ages further.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The tripartite workgroup on older workers is studying this, amongst other issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Besides legislation, the Government has also invested significant resources to provide funding and transformative support for older Singaporeans and their employers that help them adjust and stay relevant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The amount of Workfare payouts, which supplement the income of lower-income workers, is higher for older workers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have also provided extensive support for seniors to reskill and upskill, so that they can continue to contribute in the workplace.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For instance, the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy offers additional subsidies for older workers enrolling in courses pre-approved by MOE and SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The measures that I have mentioned encourage and support employers to send their older workers for training, as Mr Patrick Tay has urged earlier.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Seniors can also advance their own skills and training by using their SkillsFuture Credits.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They can choose from many courses, like those offered by the Silver Infocomm Junctions, to equip them with basic digital knowledge.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These skills can facilitate their entry into the platform economy and possible freelance opportunities, as suggested by Mr Henry Kwek earlier.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition to direct monetary support, I agree with Mr Henry Kwek, Ms Rahayu Mahzam, Mr Zainal Sapari and Dr Teo Ho Pin that we need more companies to take concrete actions in redesigning jobs and improving the working environment for our older workers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Workpro Age Management Grant and Job Redesign Grant help employers implement age-friendly practices and restructure jobs to make them easier, safer and smarter for mature employees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This not only benefits the seniors, but is also a win-win for companies, as they stand to gain from the rich experiences and expertise of an older workforce.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I asked them and they told me the average age of their 300 employees is 65.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: There is no compulsory retirement and its staff can enjoy the same pay even after they turn 62 years old.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Their oldest employees are trolley service officers, Mr Ng Kay Keng and Mr Tan Siak Hwee, are both 83 years young.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They have been with Smarte Carte for four-and-a-half years now and they like the company's age-friendly practices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And I tell Members, Smart Carte really put in the efforts to make it very senior-friendly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They redesign work processes for their mature workers and use mainly diagrammes and videos to train the seniors in bite-sized sessions for easy learning.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Supervisors also tailor their pre-shift briefings to reinforce processes and key messages that are important for our older workers' safety and security.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We recognise that as more Singaporeans grow older, and we all will get there someday, some of us, like Speaker had mentioned earlier, are members of the Merdeka Generation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, there needs to be adjustments to new work aspirations, retirement and care plans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Minister for Manpower Mrs Josephine Teo announced the formation of the Tripartite Workgroup (TWG) on Older Workers mid last year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The TWG on older workers was tasked to study key issues, such as the retirement and re-employment age as well as CPF contribution rates for older workers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In the last eight months, we have gathered the feedback and input of more than 500 people – older and younger workers, union leaders, human resource professionals, SME employers, trade associations, industry associations and various stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The exercise revealed diverse wishes that need to be balanced against the needs and expectations of different stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For instance, while older workers desire to work for as long as they can and are able to, younger workers share with us that they do worry about how that may affect their career progression.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Or while employers may want to retain their older workers, these employees may not want to continue at the same intensity as before.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, they may want to spend more time with their grandchildren or pursue certain aspirations that they have always wanted to due to their changing life goals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: All of these views gathered over the last eight months are valuable and important.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And I want to assure Members, and also Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Faisal Manap, that it is the aim of the TWG to work towards a balanced win-win outcome.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We need to strike a healthy balance among meeting the aspirations of our older and younger workers, the need for organisational renewal, redesign jobs, as many Members have spoken about, and how wages and benefits can be flexibly adjusted so that Singapore can continue to retain our attractiveness as a business and also investment location.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Beyond supporting our older workforce, we also recognise the caregiving needs that have emerged with our ageing population.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many Members have spoken about it over the last three hours.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We understand that more Singaporeans are having to balance their work with caregiving responsibilities they shoulder for their dependants and loved ones.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And we want to assure Members, including Dr Lily Neo, Dr Chia Shi-Lu, Mr Christopher de Souza, Mr Melvin Yong, Ms Rahayu Mahzam, Mr Chen Show Mao and Ms Tin Pei Ling, that MOM and also our tripartite partners are strongly committed to providing caregivers with the necessary workplace support so that they can fulfil their work and personal responsibilities and commitments, including their caregiving commitments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To better understand the needs of caregivers, Senior Minister of State for Health Edwin Tong led a cross-agency review and engaged stakeholders, including employers and caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The working caregivers whom we interviewed indicated that FWAs – and Senior Minister of State Edwin Tong spoke about it – would be a sustainable solution to help them balance their work and caregiving commitments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As Mr Henry Kwek and Dr Lily Neo pointed out, employers also have an interest to support employees' FWA needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Based on MOM's 2018 Conditions of Employment Report, it was found that among the various workplace practices, the provision of FWAs had the greatest impact on staff retention.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, for a talent choosing to join company A or B, FWA features heavily in their consideration in choosing which company to take up.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through the concerted efforts of the tripartite partners, Members, including Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Melvin Yong, Mr Christopher de Souza and Ms Rahayu Mahzam, will be pleased to know that, compared to five years ago, more workplaces are now supportive of FWAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Across the sectors, more companies are providing a greater variety of FWAs as they recognise that workers have varying FWA needs at different stages of their lives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: A worker may never know when they will need FWA.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In particular, if they have to care for ageing parents, parents-in-law or even younger kids, it gives them peace of mind knowing that if they put in a request, the company will provide.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Besides their wish for FWAs, working caregivers also expressed their need to be able to take time-off whenever necessary to care for their dependants and loved ones.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I am glad to note that there has been progress on this front.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Dr Lily Neo, Dr Chia Shi-Lu and Mr Christopher de Souza have called for legislating caregivers' leave.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Senior Minister of State Edwin Tong earlier spoke about it as well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: While we understand the reasons for this suggestion, the caregivers from our recent engagement tell us that their key requirement is not so much as to have one or two more days of leave, but to have the flexibility and ability to take some time off when the urgent need arises.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The tripartite partners had also pointed out that having more legislated leave on top of the existing leave provisions could add cost to businesses, and this could inadvertently affect the employability of those with caregiving responsibilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To this end, it is our priority to encourage employers to provide more FWAs to meet their employees' non-work needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Employers who do so with understanding and care really stand to gain from the improved loyalty and productivity of their staff.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Take the example of Angilay Davy, who is also known as Angie, a 60-year-old full-time trainer with aAdvantage Consulting Group.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Angie is the primary caregiver to her elderly sister.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is quite similar to many of the profiles that we have shared in the last three hours.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: She has to bring her sister to hospital appointments regularly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To support Angie in her caregiving duties, aAdvantage lets her have the flexibility to work from home and to take a few hours off work, when necessary.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Her co-workers support her by covering her work when she is unable to attend client meetings or conduct trainings due to her caregiving duties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This company conducts a lot of trainings for their clients.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Such an FWA is a win-win for both employer and employee. aAdvantage is able to retain valuable employees like Angie and, in Angie, many other employees also see this as an organisation that cares.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, it really inspires, not just in Angie, but the rest of the staff they have in the organisation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They manage to retain valuable employees like Angie, who is an asset with her many years of experience.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Caregivers like Angie can continue to be a productive employee while meeting the care needs of her sister.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have talked quite a bit about FWA.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We recognise that FWAs are not one-off solutions, but they are really long-term practices sustained by a supportive workplace culture.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I agree with Dr Chia Shi-Lu that schemes must not be onerous administratively such that it deters adoption.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Therefore, the Work-Life Grant was recently enhanced to make it easier for the employers to qualify.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To enable more companies to benefit from the Work-Life Grant and to make FWA adoption more pervasive, MOM is exploring to increase the Work-Life Grant budget.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: More details will be shared at the MOM Committee of Supply next month.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will also continue to encourage more companies to adopt the relevant Tripartite Standards and publicly commit to progressive workplace practices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I agree with Dr Lily Neo that Government agencies should take the lead, and I am pleased to share that adopters of the Tripartite Standards include those in the public sector.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our efforts to promote the adoption of FWAs are showing positive effects.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Henry Kwek suggested studying and learning from FWA legislation of other countries to promote greater FWA adoption.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will need to examine the potential impact and effectiveness of any FWA legislation before considering a model which is suitable for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Having a legislated right to request FWA may not necessarily improve adoption of FWAs if companies are not able to restructure their jobs or workplace arrangements to accede to the FWA requests.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The key is to better support and enable the companies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We are mindful that FWAs could affect business operations and we would not want to inadvertently affect the employability of the staff who are requesting for FWAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: FWAs help working caregivers juggle their work and caregiving responsibilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: However, depending on the level of care required by their loved ones, some caregivers may leave the workforce temporarily or even longer periods.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many of our Members have cited examples in your ward.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Those who have been away for a long period of time may need additional help to find jobs, but they may not be familiar with the existing employment support they can get.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will raise greater awareness of the Adapt and Grow initiative that offers a suite of services and programmes to facilitate employment matching and help jobseekers overcome mismatches in skills, wages or job expectations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure Members and also Mr Melvin Yong that MOM and MOH will, in the second half of 2019, be reaching out to caregivers who wish to return to the workforce.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will do so through various touchpoints, such as AICare Links, operated by AIC.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Dr Intan Mokhtar asked to raise the CPF contribution rate for members age 55 and above.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The TWG on Older Workers is currently studying the CPF contribution rates for members aged 55 and above.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For self-employed persons (SEPs), we are going to make it easier for them to make MediSave contributions by implementing a "contribute-as-you-earn" model.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government, as a service buyer, will take the lead to pilot this with our self-employed contractors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: After addressing the challenges, the SEPs faced with MediSave contributions, we will then review how SEPs can also contribute to their CPF Special Account.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Members, including Mr Henry Kwek, Mr Chen Show Mao and Ms Anthea Ong, have voiced their concerns about improving the retirement adequacy of caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We recognise that some full-time caregivers may not have been able to work in their younger years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They may, therefore, not have much CPF savings for retirement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is where the Silver Support Scheme can come in.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Silver Support Scheme supplements the retirement incomes of elderly Singaporeans who had low earnings throughout their lives and currently have little or no family support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For those with family members who can top up their CPF savings, the Government has lowered the minimum threshold sum required to make it easier for CPF members to transfer their CPF savings to their spouses, parents and grandparents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will enable more members to strengthen the retirement adequacy of their loved ones.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We are encouraged by the positive response to this move.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira made three suggestions: first, he proposed to strengthen Silver Support Scheme; second, he suggested topping up the CPF accounts of members with low contributions; and finally, he asked for the Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme (LRIS) to be introduced soon.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: First, we are concerned about the elderly who may not have enough retirement income.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: However, it is also important to place this in context.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The vast majority of our elderly own their own homes and have family support and personal savings to rely on.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For those with lower income throughout their lives, and have little or no family support in retirement, we have, as I said earlier, the Silver Support Scheme to supplement their retirement incomes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And I want to assure Assoc Prof Walter Theseira we will review the Silver Support Scheme from time to time to ensure that it continues to provide meaningful support for this group of elderly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: At the same time, we have to balance this with the need to ensure that the entire system remains fiscally sustainable in the long run.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Second, we already supplement CPF contributions of the lower income via the WIS Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have taken this approach because, as a society, we want to encourage work and employment and, earlier on, we heard from many Members that many of the seniors that you spoke to, they want to work for various reasons: financial independence, for passion, for purpose.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I remember Mr Patrick Tay spoke about the example that he mentioned "he wants to work because it allows him to be physically and mentally sharp".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, as a society, we embrace this and we have uplifted the wages of the lower income and kept employment high and then unemployment low.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For those unable to help themselves for various reasons, we want to make sure a safety net is there to support them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We want to make sure that those who cannot work and have no support, the Government will provide for their basic needs and, if necessary, give them the long-term support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And this is where the whole-of-Government will have to step in, such as MOM, MSF, and Members have heard from Senior Parliamentary Secretary for National Development Sun Xueling as well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Third, CPF interest rates are already high, compared to other market instruments, on a risk-adjusted basis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure Assoc Prof Walter Theseira that we are studying LRIS carefully.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: However, developing an investment product, especially as you can see what happened in the last 10 years with investment products, especially the sophisticated ones, developing an investment product is a complex effort and we have to carefully balance the risks undertaken by our members and the expected returns.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, we want to assure Assoc Prof Walter Theseira that we will certainly update on LRIS in due course.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, overall, we have a system that strikes a balance between adequacy in retirement, support for the lower-income seniors, especially those who have low balances in their CPF accounts, and also longer-term fiscal sustainability, and we have achieved good results in retirement adequacy with comparable replacement rates to other OECD countries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: While we are constantly looking for ways to do better, we should build on what has been working well for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Talking about CPF, we have also been going out there to get feedback from members, and we recognise that some people may find the different CPF schemes and requirements fairly mindboggling.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This year, CRPS is available to those turning 65.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As Mr Henry Kwek suggested earlier, we will also work with community partners to provide services that help older Singaporeans plan for their financial milestones and better prepare for retirement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, Mr Speaker, Sir, indeed, a whole-of-society effort is necessary for Singaporeans to age with purpose, to age with dignity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Increasingly, continued employment is becoming a key aspiration of ageing meaningfully.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It is our common goal to support our seniors so that our seniors can continue to contribute to the economy and the community for as long as they are able to and wish to.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will do all we can to make our workplace supportive of Singaporeans who need to balance caregiving responsibilities alongside their work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure Members that there will be no let-up in MOM's efforts to foster age-friendly and progressive work practices among employers. "Age-smart" companies stand to gain when they start thinking about creating alternative career routes for older workers and also providing more FWAs and schedules for them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, on this note, Mr Speaker, Sir, I support both Motions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We agree with the suggestions made by many hon Members that seniors should be involved in the wider community, be it through volunteerism, sports or the arts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our seniors may have transited out of the workforce, but they continue to have much to offer due to their wealth of life experiences and skillsets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Through volunteerism, seniors can also reap benefits, such as sustained social and mental wellness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: At the same time, they will serve as inspirations and role models for future generations and strengthen our society through norms and values.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In fact, our seniors have been shown to be far more avid and consistent at volunteering than younger age groups!

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We agree with the recommendation made by Members to provide more support for seniors’ volunteer efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue to grow partnerships with community partners to engage more seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MCCY has already been working alongside a number of organisations that help match seniors to volunteering activities according to their interests, availability and preferred locations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue to support RSVP and similar groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: NVPC has been exploring partnerships with learning institutions and community organisations that run courses for older PMETs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Through such partnerships, older PMETs can be connected to volunteer opportunities where they can apply their newly acquired skills, such as community gardening or befriending.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As Mr Ang Wei Neng has raised, senior volunteers can provide valuable advisory services to VWOs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We agree that the Centre for Non-Profit Leadership's (CNPL's) BoardMatch Programme is doing good work in reaching out to committed and highly qualified professionals across various industries and sectors and identifying candidates who are able to serve non-profit organisations in a leadership capacity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There are many opportunities for such volunteers to help with building up governance capabilities and bringing fresh perspectives to the non-profit sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Senior volunteerism is an integral part of the larger SG Cares movement where we want to grow care and inclusivity in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We hope to identify more champions from various walks of life who can rally fellow seniors to serve in their communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also support the recommendation to encourage seniors to take greater ownership of their health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue to dedicate more resources to cater to their needs in the area of sport and exercise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Beyond the ActiveSG Masters Programme mentioned in the report, we also have Active Health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is a national social movement that goes beyond healthcare to health, to celebrate living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To kickstart their journey, seniors can visit an Active Health Lab for a free onboarding session to assess their health status and fitness level.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Active Health experts will then work with them to set personal health and wellness goals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Seniors can then get active by participating in programmes at our ActiveSG centres and Sport-in-Precinct facilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There are also Active Health Mobile Labs deployed across the island for those who do not live near an Active Health Lab.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Living better through sports is not limited to physical activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It includes community roles for seniors who can sign up to be Team Nila volunteers at the ActiveSG centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They can serve as sports or Active Health champions, where they have opportunities to meet like-minded volunteers while they galvanise the community to get active.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MCCY is also working with SportSG to ensure that our sporting spaces are designed to cater to our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, at the upcoming ActiveSG gym in Ang Mo Kio Community Centre, seniors can participate in elder-friendly exercise programmes when it opens later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will make sure all our ActiveSG gyms provide an environment that is safe and accessible for our active agers and furnished with equipment that is suitable for their usage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There will also be qualified staff onsite to provide any assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is important to involve our seniors in our arts and heritage, too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This can improve their quality of life, while enriching our cultural offerings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As pointed out by Mr Terence Ho, the arts can play an important role in building social bonds and increasing mental well-being as we age.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MCCY, the National Arts Council (NAC) and National Heritage Board (NHB) are working very closely with the arts community and other partners from the social service and healthcare sectors on programmes that are accessible and relevant to our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The 2018 Festival featured a community arts project between youths and seniors from NTUC Health Active Ageing Hub at Kampung Admiralty, which included an installation and performance on the theme of "happiness".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In addition, our Heritage Institutions serve as Silver Hubs to promote active ageing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This kit includes images of significant landmarks and artefacts, prompting the exchange of personal memories and intergenerational dialogues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MCCY, NAC and NHB will continue with these efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We want to ensure that our seniors have ample opportunities to participate in our arts and culture landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In Mandarin):  	Mr Speaker, Sir, Singapore's social structure is changing rapidly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As the average age of our population rises, MCCY will endeavour to help our seniors live an active, healthy, meaningful and fulfilling life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We plan to create more opportunities and channels for seniors to participate in volunteer work, sports and arts activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Arts and culture will not only help seniors to communicate more but also improve the quality of their lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MCCY, NAC and NHB have been working with arts groups, social workers and healthcare organisations to launch arts activities suitable for seniors so that they can enjoy their golden years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Of course, having good health is also very important.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In English): Let me now conclude in English, Mr Speaker.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Many of our seniors want to continue making a positive impact to society and remain active and connected throughout their silver years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We recognise that they have much to offer for future generations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Hence, we must support them as best as we can and involve them in the community in ways that are meaningful and fulfilling.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Before I wrap up, I just want to share an observation.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Thereafter, I will put the Question in respect of each Motion to the House for voting.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Your passion and thoughtful remarks are much appreciated.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Today, we spoke about boldly reframing our narrative to a positive agenda, because while ageing brings a set of challenges, it also brings many exciting possibilities.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: In fact, Mr Mohamed Irshad mentioned that 70 is the new 60.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Also, given the diverse and evolving generations of future seniors, we call for the Government to continue engagements and dialogues, especially through the spirit of Our Singapore Conversation.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Members are also in agreement that most seniors find purpose through work and bring much to the table.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: And according to Mr Patrick Tay, seniors are treasure troves of experience and expertise.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: With regard to employment for seniors, Members noted that we are generally in a good position.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Mr Zainal Sapari recommended employers adopt proper rest areas at worksites and environmentally-friendly equipment and technology so that work becomes safer and easier for seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Dr Intan Mokhtar asked to raise the retirement and re-employment age.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Our seniors, especially the Merdeka Generation, possess a wealth of knowledge and energy.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Members, including Ms Joan Pereira and Er Dr Lee Bee Wah shared that many seniors want to contribute and not solely be beneficiaries.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Ms Joan Pereira called for hospitals, museums, schools and VWOs to recruit more senior volunteers.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Members also asked both public and private organisations to help our seniors stay integrated with society.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Mr Terence Ho made compelling points about ageing well through the arts and asked for more support for the whole of Singapore in getting seniors to do art.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Mayor Teo Ho Pin called for HPB to provide a dedicated endowment for CDCs to fund active ageing so that this national movement has more legs.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng suggested PA to take a harder look to explore more "work-based" activities that naturally attract more men, given that grassroots volunteers attract largely women.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: And Mr Mohamed Irshad called for more intergenerational bonding so that we can harness the collective wisdom of our seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: There is a saying that, "We shape the building, thereafter the building shapes us".

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Members spoke at length about housing and affordable assisted living (AL) services.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Dr Lily Neo spoke about not just the importance of affordable AL services, but also her own experience building such a service in Tanjong Pagar.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Ms Joan Pereira spoke about SACs that serve seniors beyond rental flat residents.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: She also spoke about more flexibility in rental flat eligibility to help more seniors facing diverse needs and putting in key aspects of the Lasting Power of Attorney and Will into our HDB processes.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam spoke about having more group homes with AL facilities in both public and private housing, and more flexibility and compassion in assessing eligibility in our rental housing programmes.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: In today’s debate, Members noted that Singapore has undergone one of the most aggressive healthcare and healthcare financing system expansions and transformations in any developed country in recent memory and we can continue to build on that.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Therefore, Ms Rahayu Mahzam asked MOH to exercise more discretion regarding CHAS eligibility to factor in changing income and family circumstances.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked for a review on the funding model for nursing homes and cautioned against a race to the bottom.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Mr Darryl David asked for a whole-of-Singapore effort to active ageing and healthy living, a point he made so passionately.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Dr Intan Mokhtar spoke about encouraging more Singaporeans to practise medicine, especially to serve our seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Members also spoke about making our transportation more senior-friendly.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Mr Faisal Manap asked for an update on the implementation of Silver Zones so that seniors can commute with peace of mind.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Miss Cheryl Chan asked for an innovative transportation mode in private estates for seniors, a point that I also agree with.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Members also spoke about the importance of individual responsibility.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: But as family nucleus continues to shrink, Ms Joan Pereira asked for a holistic policy review to remove obstacles for extended families to provide support for seniors should they choose to.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Members also discussed how to help seniors to be digitally ready.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling stressed the importance of designing to include.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Mr Darryl David spoke about partnering IHLs to promote digital literacy and creating affordable senior-centric smartphones.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Members also spoke about seniors in need of financial support.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Of course, in any society, there will be those who fall through the cracks.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Therefore, Mr Faisal Manap also touched on the issue of elderly suicide and asked for a closer look at this issue.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: He also questioned whether we could do more for frail seniors who feel compelled to work, doing tasks, such as cardboard collecting.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: One of the ways to help seniors in need is to strengthen the retirement adequacy of seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: We note employers' concerns on rising cost, and the Government can help by not withdrawing their support for grants for older workers and senior retirees.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: I also spoke about better incentives so that seniors can choose to defer their CPF payout withdrawals and also on the importance of strengthening financial literacy.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira spoke about finetuning the CPF to provide a basic retirement payout, incentives to improve contribution rates and better returns on investments.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Beyond supporting our seniors in need through financial assistance, local programmes also help multiply and deepen the impact of Government policies.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: And Members today spoke at length on the various ways, as leaders of this nation in various capacities, we collectively coordinate local efforts for seniors in need.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: For me, this is the most inspiring part of our debate because needs express what words cannot.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Mr Murali Pillai shared about how his volunteers assist caregivers to seniors with mental issues, such as dementia.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: He also built up a team of health peers for residents.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: A team from Kembangan-Chai Chee, where Speaker Tan Chuan-Jin serves, partners AIC and IMH to also help families with mental illnesses.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: In Henderson-Dawson, where Ms Joan Pereira serves, residents work with Willing Hearts to provide daily meals to neighbours in need, including many seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Mayor Teo Ho Pin shared on the very comprehensive programme that Northwest District has implemented to keep our seniors active and healthy.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah shared that in Nee Soon South, there are two cafes where seniors gather, and this makes it easy for VWOs to engage them.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Nee Soon South also has a free volunteer-run aromatherapy and massage centre for caregivers and is building a dementia-friendly community.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng and Mayor Teo Ho Pin both shared that —

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: And Mr Ang Wei Neng and Mayor Teo Ho Pin both shared that as chairpersons of their Town Council respectively, they took extra effort to take on older workers.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: I shared Kebun Baru's comprehensive programme to take care of frail and socially isolated seniors through befriending, medical attention, free-meal deliveries, healthy communal meals and stepped-up Police patrols.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: I also shared on our SAC and church gathering points serving all seniors, our cancer peer support network and efforts to build a dementia-friendly Kebun Baru.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Now that I have summarised our discussion, let me thank Senior Minister of State Amy Khor, Senior Minister of State Sim Ann, Senior Minister of State Edwin Tong, Minister of State Sam Tan, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Low Yen Ling and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Sun Xueling for providing a comprehensive response on behalf of the Government and for taking on some ideas immediately.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: In my conversations with Senior Minister of State Amy Khor, she frequently described our whole-of-Government plan for active ageing as a "Living Document", one with ample room for new good ideas.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Indeed, her comment reflects the open-mindedness of our Government.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: I am confident that our Government will review our ideas closely and take in many of them in good time.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: At this juncture, I would also like to thank retired Members of Parliament, Mdm Yu-Foo Yee Shoon, Assoc Prof Koo Tsai Kee and Dr Chiang Hai Ding, who, in the best tradition of PAP.SG, passed down invaluable knowledge on senior policies from earlier generations of PAP Members of Parliament to current Members of Parliament, such as Ms Joan Pereira and myself.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Getting Singapore and Singaporeans prepared for successful ageing requires long-term planning.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: This is our strength and we must leverage it.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: This requires us to develop the necessary policies and mindset beyond today and tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: But PAP.SG also believes that all of us, wearing different hats, whether it is employers, employees, unions, social workers and seniors, must all come together and play our role.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: No single group can succeed without the others moving together.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: And one day, we ourselves will age, and we, too, deserve nothing less.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Clearly, it is neither sustainable, practicable nor desirable for all caregiving to be relegated to the state or to delegated institutions.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: This twin Motion today is united by a focus on the elderly, and caring for our seniors is an issue of particular relevance in the context of our rapidly ageing society.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: All Members agree that a whole-of-society approach is needed.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: All of us – the Government, the community, families and individuals – need to work together to support our senior care recipients and also their caregivers, who are often elderly as well.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Caregivers face many hurdles, as Members have elaborated in some detail.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: But the one key problem that most caregivers face, and which has been described by many studies on caregivers, is financial.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: This would certainly help to alleviate the out-of-pocket expenditures of family caregivers.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: The financial and, indeed, the physical and mental stress faced by caregivers is compounded by disruptions to their work due to their caregiving commitments.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: And, as noted, close to three-quarters of caregivers are employed.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Mr Melvin Yong has recommended a Progressive Wage Model (PWM) for professional caregivers and also asked for more to be done to support caregivers’ re-entry into the workforce.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: I believe that more can be done to leverage schemes, such as Adapt and Grow, to support their re-entry into the workforce.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Like Mr Melvin Yong, Mr Christopher de Souza and Dr Lily Neo, I also hope that MOM will reconsider legislating caregiver or eldercare leave for workers.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Today, in this House, we have heard many touching and inspirational stories of caring and being cared for, and Members' support for this Motion in this House today signifies Members' appreciation and recognition of the sacrifices and selflessness of all caregivers.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: And we have to do more to support caregivers, other than just financial support.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Many caregivers feel isolated and overwhelmed at various points in their caregiving journey, and burnout and depression are all too common amongst caregivers.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: The home-based respite service to support caregivers for cancer patients, as also announced by Senior Minister of State Edwin Tong, will also go a long way towards improving end-of-life care for Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: AIC’s pilot outreach teams to reach out to caregivers who are themselves at risk, and the moves towards growing caregiver support networks in our neighbourhoods, are all welcome moves to safeguard the well-being of caregivers and, in turn, those that they care for.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: I note, however, that the Survey on Informal Caregiving that was commissioned by MCYS and published in the early 2010s, noted that while recognising that support networks are likely to be important, the participation by caregivers in such networks was low and the overall experience reported was not particularly positive.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: I hope that we can learn from these past experiences such that the current incarnation of caregiver support networks will meet with greater acceptance and greater success.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Informal caregiving means that caregivers are typically not formally trained in caregiving, and often have their roles thrust upon them when a loved one falls ill, often quite unexpectedly.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Many caregivers have shared that one of the reasons they feel unable to cope is because they have little experience and little knowledge about how to look after someone else in a proper and efficient manner.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: In a similar vein, we recognise that, in Singapore, a high proportion of informal caregiving is provided by FDWs, who also often do not have such skills.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Hence, the measures that were announced to broaden caregiver training are very welcome indeed.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Besides skills, many caregivers have also shared that they often had difficulties finding about formal support services that could have facilitated their caregiving duties.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: In hospitals, we have patient or care navigators to assist patients in accessing the types of care and support that they need, and this has paid significant dividends in improving the standard of patient care and the overall care experience, and improved value while reducing costs.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: E-services, as suggested by Mr Melvin Yong, can also be used to push out information to caregivers and assist caregivers to procure services and equipment.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: On a similar note, Ms Denise Phua has also spoken about the special challenges facing caregivers of PWDs and a call for better case identification, individualisation and integration bears a closer look.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: All of us here are caregivers, either at present, in the past or in the future.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Caring for others is an important determinant of who we are as individuals, and who we are as a society.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We have now come to the conclusion of the debate.
